jobs.title: Principal, Power Systems & Data Centers - Impact Consulting
jobs.excerpt: Job Description: RMI is an independent, nonpartisan nonprofit working to transform global energy systems and align markets with a clean, resilient, and prosperous future.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

RMI is an independent, nonpartisan nonprofit working to transform global energy systems and align markets with a clean, resilient, and prosperous future. We partner with businesses, financial institutions, policymakers, and communities to accelerate solutions that unlock the energy transition at scale.

Position Overview

RMI is seeking a Principal, Power Systems & Data Centers to build and lead RMI’s cross-program strategy and advisory work focused on the rapidly growing data center sector.

The growth of AI and digital infrastructure is creating significant challenges and opportunities across electricity systems, generation and transmission, buildings, industrial materials, water, backup power, site selection, permitting, finance, and community engagement. Addressing these issues requires expertise that spans traditional organizational and sector boundaries.

RMI has deep capabilities across many of these areas, distributed across its Electricity, Buildings, Industries, Intelligence, Climate Finance, Third Derivative, US Program, and other sector and geography teams. The Principal will serve as an integrating leader across these capabilities — establishing RMI’s institutional theory of change for data centers, translating that strategy into differentiated market offerings, developing relationships and opportunities with priority external partners and clients, and leading complex cross-program engagements.

The position will sit within RMI’s Impact Consulting - Delivery Excellence Team and work horizontally across the Institute.

The successful candidate will combine meaningful data center industry expertise with strong strategic judgment, commercial orientation, consulting and delivery capabilities, and the ability to influence and mobilize teams across organizational boundaries.

Application Deadline: Sunday, October 4th at 11:59pm U.S. Central Time

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Thought Leadership

  • Develop and maintain RMI’s institutional theory of change for data centers, defining how rapid digital infrastructure growth affects the energy transition and where RMI can have the greatest impact.

  • Identify the most important system-level barriers, leverage points, and interventions needed to align data center growth with clean energy deployment, grid reliability, affordability, decarbonization, and community outcomes.

  • Establish a clear view of where RMI should play based on its technical expertise, market influence, analytical capabilities, convening power, and external relationships.

  • Integrate perspectives from Electricity, Buildings, Industries, Intelligence, Climate Finance, Third Derivative, Transportation, policy, and other relevant teams into a coherent RMI data center strategy.

  • Identify priority stakeholders whose decisions RMI should seek to influence, including hyperscalers, colocation providers, developers, utilities, regulators, policymakers, investors, and communities.

  • Define strategic and reputational guardrails for RMI’s data center work, including where RMI should — and should not — pursue commercial engagements.

  • Monitor changing technology, market, policy, infrastructure, and investment conditions and adapt RMI’s strategy accordingly.

  • Represent RMI as a senior thought leader on the intersection of data center growth, energy infrastructure, and the clean energy transition.

Market Development & External Engagement

  • Develop and execute RMI’s data center go-to-market strategy, translating the institutional theory of change into a focused set of commercial and partnership opportunities.

  • Define priority client segments, buyers, pain points, and decisions where RMI has a differentiated right to win.

  • Develop and market-test a portfolio of commercial offering hypotheses with external stakeholders and prospective clients.

  • Identify and cultivate relationships with hyperscalers, colocation providers, developers, utilities, infrastructure investors, technology providers, and other priority stakeholders.

  • Conduct senior-level market and client conversations to understand emerging needs and translate those needs into actionable opportunities for RMI.

  • Partner closely with RMI’s Corporate Engagement team and program leaders to develop priority account strategies and a qualified pipeline of opportunities.

  • Shape concept notes, proposals, scopes of work, staffing plans, delivery approaches, and commercial models.

  • Apply disciplined go/no-go and right-to-win criteria to prospective engagements.

  • Support senior client discussions and negotiations through contract execution.

Potential commercial offering areas may include:

  • Power availability, procurement, and grid integration

  • Flexible load and demand-side solutions

  • Site selection and energy infrastructure strategy

  • Clean firm power and backup generation

  • Transmission and interconnection constraints

  • Data center energy and emissions strategy

  • Water use and cooling

  • Low-carbon cement, steel, and construction materials

  • Integration of Carbon Dioxide Removals (CDR) on site or adjacent to data centers

  • Sustainability standards and metric design for data centers

  • Permitting, policy, and community considerations

  • Data center financing and investment

  • Cross-sector decarbonization strategies for hyperscalers and operators

The Principal will not be expected to personally possess deep technical expertise in every area. A core requirement of the role is the ability to identify, mobilize, and integrate RMI’s subject-matter expertise into coherent strategies and client solutions.

Program Leadership & Delivery

  • Serve as the accountable engagement leader for large, strategically important data center projects spanning multiple RMI programs and capabilities.

  • Translate complex and ambiguous client questions into structured workstreams, hypotheses, analytical approaches, and decision-oriented outputs.

  • Assemble and lead multidisciplinary teams drawing on expertise from across RMI.

  • Define clear roles, responsibilities, and decision rights between the central Impact Consulting team and program-based subject-matter experts.

  • Maintain accountability for project scope, timeline, budget, quality, and client expectations.

  • Synthesize technical inputs from multiple disciplines into clear, integrated, executive-level recommendations.

  • Guide the production of rigorous, decision-grade presentations, reports, analyses, and other client deliverables.

  • Lead executive client meetings, workshops, working sessions, and presentations.

  • Identify project risks early and take corrective action before issues become client escalations.

  • Identify and shape follow-on opportunities where additional work creates genuine mission and client value.

  • Ensure lessons from delivery inform subsequent offerings, scopes, pricing, methodologies, and strategic priorities.

Cross-Program Integration & Organizational Contribution

  • Create the connective tissue required for RMI to operate as an integrated data center platform rather than a collection of independent technical teams.

  • Build strong relationships with relevant Principals, Senior Principals, Managing Directors, and subject-matter experts across the Institute.

  • Develop and maintain a clear view of RMI’s relevant capabilities, experts, analytical assets, datasets, relationships, and existing data center work.

  • Identify capability gaps that may require new analysis, external expertise, partnerships, data, or investment.

  • Develop repeatable approaches for staffing and governing multidisciplinary data center engagements.

  • Identify methodologies, analytical modules, frameworks, datasets, and deliverables that can be reused across clients and engagements.

  • Convert recurring client needs into repeatable advisory offerings where appropriate.

  • Capture and institutionalize knowledge from client engagements and external market interactions.

  • Mentor and coach RMI staff working on data center and Impact Consulting engagements.

  • Contribute to RMI’s broader leadership community and the continued development of the Institute’s Impact Consulting capabilities.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience, with substantial experience in data centers, digital infrastructure, energy infrastructure, or a closely related sector.

  • Demonstrated understanding of the data center ecosystem and meaningful experience with several of the following:

    • Hyperscale or colocation development

    • Power availability and procurement

    • Utility engagement and interconnection

    • Site selection

    • Data center design and construction

    • Sustainability and decarbonization

    • Permitting and regulatory issues

    • Water and cooling

    • Backup generation

    • Infrastructure investment

  • Proven experience developing and executing strategy in an ambiguous, rapidly evolving market.

  • Experience leading complex, senior-client-facing consulting, advisory, or strategic engagements.

  • Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop hypotheses, synthesize complex analysis, and translate technical information into actionable executive recommendations.

  • Experience developing new offerings, shaping client opportunities, and contributing to business development, proposals, or commercial pursuits.

  • Strong project and team leadership skills, including experience managing multidisciplinary workstreams, timelines, budgets, scope, and stakeholder expectations.

  • Demonstrated ability to personally develop and shape high-quality analytical and client-facing deliverables.

  • Ability to influence senior decision-makers and mobilize teams without direct reporting authority.

  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills.

  • Ability to bridge technical expertise and senior-level business decision-making across diverse stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 15+ years of professional experience with increasing strategic, commercial, and operational responsibility.

  • Graduate degree in engineering, business, economics, public policy, energy, sustainability, or a related field.

  • Direct experience working for or advising hyperscalers, colocation providers, data center developers, utilities serving large-load customers, or digital infrastructure investors.

  • Experience in strategy or management consulting focused on data centers, energy, infrastructure, technology, or sustainability.

  • Experience with data center development, site selection, energy procurement, infrastructure strategy, or investment.

  • Demonstrated success building new market offerings or business lines.

  • Strong existing network across the data center, energy, utility, technology, or infrastructure ecosystem.

  • Experience leading large, multidisciplinary initiatives involving stakeholders across multiple organizations or sectors.

  • Combination of industry operating experience and consulting/advisory experience.

Why This Role Matters

The rapid expansion of data centers represents both a major challenge and a significant opportunity for the clean energy transition.

Decisions being made today about where and how data centers are built, powered, financed, and operated will influence electricity infrastructure, capital deployment, industrial demand, community outcomes, and emissions trajectories for decades.

Few organizations have RMI’s combination of energy-system expertise, technical depth, market relationships, analytical capabilities, and convening power. At the same time, these capabilities are distributed across the Institute.

This role will be responsible for bringing those capabilities together — establishing a coherent RMI strategy for data centers, identifying where RMI can create differentiated impact, translating that strategy into concrete market interventions and client offerings, and ensuring that RMI can execute complex cross-program work at a consistently high standard.

Location

We are a remote-ready company with team members around the globe. Our beautiful and welcoming offices are available for meetings or focused work, whether you are traveling through or living nearby. Our U.S. offices are in New York City; Washington DC; Oakland, California; Boulder, Colorado, and Basalt, Colorado. This role can be located from anywhere in the continental United States.

We provide you with the essential IT equipment plus a one-time home technology payment and a monthly work from home/commuter allowance to ensure you have a comfortable home office set up and necessary supplies.

We love seeing each other in person! We occasionally gather for shared time together like retreats and learning experiences. Be ready to travel for occasional in-person meetings (and of course, we cover travel costs). Some roles may require more travel, which will be discussed during the hiring process.

Compensation

At RMI, we prioritize fairness in our pay practices. Salaries are determined based on a mix of experience, market benchmarks, and internal equity across similar roles. The salary range of this position is $139,823-$172,332. New hires typically start toward the lower end of the range, depending on experience and alignment with the role’s scope. In addition to base salary, this position includes an annual bonus target of 20% and eligibility for merit-based increases, which are tied to both individual and organizational performance.

Benefits

RMI offers a comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • 403(b) retirement match with immediate vesting

  • Group life, AD&D, and short- and long-term disability coverage

  • Health savings or flexible spending accounts

  • Fertility and hormonal health support

  • Mental health and wellness support

  • Comprehensive leaves of absence, including parental leave

  • Generous paid time off and sick leave

  • Regional and organization-wide holidays

  • Work-from-home and home technology allowances

  • Learning and development opportunities

  • Potential for bonuses and merit increases

  • Remote and hybrid work options

  • Team gatherings and regional meetups

  • Rewards and recognition programs

Diversity

We know that the diversity of our teams makes us stronger as an organization, and RMI is dedicated to the principles of equal employment opportunity as outlined in U.S. federal law. We prohibit discrimination against applicants, interns, and employees on the basis of any legally recognized basis, including but not limited to: age (40 and over), race, color, sex, pregnancy (including lactation, childbirth, or related medical conditions), religion, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing and characteristics), sexual orientation, gender expression/identity, uniformed service member status, veteran status, citizenship status, or any other applicable status protected by applicable law.

RMI is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Instacart+ is Instacart's membership program, the connective tissue between the brand and its most loyal, high-value customers. With benefits like $0 delivery fees, partner perks, and exclusive savings, Instacart+ is the foundation of our long-term customer relationship strategy. Members shop more, spend more, and stay longer, and this role is responsible for making sure more customers become Instacart+ members and realize the benefits of doing so.

We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the full go-to-market strategy for Instacart+. You'll shape how we position, message, and grow the membership program from acquisition campaigns that convert first-timers to lifecycle strategies that deepen engagement with existing members. This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role at the intersection of product, brand, and growth.

The ideal candidate has deep roots in subscription or loyalty marketing, having grown a membership program, driven retention through value communication, and knows how to make the math of membership feel like a no-brainer to a consumer. You bring both the analytical rigor to understand what's working and the storytelling instinct to make it resonate. This role reports to the Director, Consumer Product Marketing.

What you'll cook up in your first year

  • Own the Instacart+ differentiated positioning that sets it apart from competing membership and subscription offerings.
  • Members have a reason to stay: you've identified the moments where member value is highest and built messaging and lifecycle programs that bring those moments to life across email, push, in-app, and paid.
  • Acquisition is measurably stronger: you've partnered with growth and performance marketing teams to develop and test messaging frameworks that convert trial users and lapsed members into committed subscribers.
  • The product roadmap reflects member insights: you've become the internal voice of the Instacart+ member, bringing qualitative and quantitative research into roadmap conversations that shape what gets built next.
  • New Instacart+ features launch with best-in-class GTM plans: you own the brief, the messaging, and the channel strategy from kickoff through post-launch performance review.
  • Senior stakeholders and XFN partners trust you as the category expert: you've developed a compelling POV on the subscription and loyalty landscape and use it to sharpen the Instacart+ strategy.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in marketing, with at least 4+ years in product marketing; experience at a consumer tech company is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated track record owning GTM strategy for a subscription, membership, or loyalty program, from positioning through lifecycle, with measurable results.
  • Deep fluency in subscription/loyalty marketing mechanics: you understand member acquisition, onboarding, engagement, and churn, and know how to use marketing to move each lever.
  • A sharp strategic mind that can synthesize consumer research, behavioral data, and competitive signals into positioning and messaging that cuts through
  • Proven ability to influence product roadmaps. You've brought the voice of the customer into planning cycles and shaped what gets built, not just how it gets marketed.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting and defending strategy to VP and C-suite stakeholders.
  • Experience partnering closely with growth, lifecycle/CRM, creative, and data science teams to develop and execute multi-channel campaigns
  • Proficient in using data and A/B testing to develop and iterate on messaging; as comfortable in a metrics dashboard as in a creative brief
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Optional garnishes

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience marketing a subscription or loyalty program in a marketplace or two-sided platform context (e.g., retail, food delivery, grocery)
  • Background working on programs with tiered benefits, earn/burn mechanics, or partner integrations
  • Experience running or partnering on member research, including surveys, focus groups, UXR to surface insights that directly inform strategy
  • Prior experience managing or mentoring PMMs or junior marketers
  • Familiarity with the grocery or CPG retail marketing landscape

tätigkeit & voraussetzungen

  • Umfassende Einarbeitung
  • Laufende Betreuung durch Deinen persönlichen Coach und regelmäßige Schulungen
  • Entlohnung:
    Während der Einarbeitung (2 bis 4 Wochen): 7,50 € / Telefoniestunde* sowie einer Provision von 7,00 € pro stattgefundenem Termin
    Nach erfolgreicher Einarbeitung: 10,00 € / Telefoniestunde* (bei Erreichen unseres Mindestziels von 1 Termin alle 2 Stunden)

    Provision: 6,00 € bis 11,00 € pro Termin

    Zusatz-Bonus: 15,00 € je erfolgreichem Verkauf aus einem Termin

  • Top-Terminierer: ca. 15 bis 20 € pro Telefoniestunde
* Telefoniestunde besteht aus Anwahl und Gesprächsdauer inkl. Anrufbeantworter

faq

Worum geht es bei uns?
Wir suchen Mitarbeitende, die im Home-Office für uns telefonieren. Wir sind eine Online Marketing Agentur, die seit über 25 Jahren auf dem Markt ist. Unsere Kunden sind kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen, denen es wichtig ist, in den Suchmaschinen von ihren Kunden gut gefunden zu werden. Dafür bieten wir verschiedene Marketinginstrumente an. In diesem Projekt bieten wir unseren Kunden eine kostenlose Wettbewerbsanalyse mit einer kostenlosen Beratung an. Erfahre mehr über uns: OMERGY/INTRAG

Was wird benötigt?
Wir stellen Dir unseren Dialer mit unseren Datensätzen zur Verfügung. Du benötigst lediglich einen funktionsfähigen Windows Rechner mit Windows 11 und eine sehr gute Internetleitung.
Zudem benötigst Du ein Headset zur Telefonie.
Zur Einrichtung Deines Rechners erhältst Du Unterstützung von uns.

Wie sieht der Arbeitsablauf aus?
Du meldest Dich an einer Software an, die lokal auf Deinem Rechner installiert wird, einem sogenannten Dialer. Über diesen Dialer bekommst Du vorqualifizierte Adressen von uns und telefonierst dann mit dem Dialer über das Internet.

Wie läuft die Einarbeitung?
Für die Einarbeitung benötigen wir in der Regel drei Tage, mit jeweils einer Stunde Einarbeitungszeit pro Tag über Microsoft Teams. In dieser Zeit erhältst Du einen ausreichenden Einblick, um den Kunden erklären zu können, worum es bei dem Angebot geht. Zudem erhältst Du natürlich einen Gesprächsleitfaden, Beispielgespräche und unsere Unterstützung, so dass wir schnell in dem Projekt starten können. Es erfolgt auch nach der Einarbeitungszeit eine Betreuung in der Gruppe über Microsoft Teams.

Wann wird das Geld überwiesen?
Jeweils zum Monatsanfang wird von Dir eine Rechnung für den vorangegangenen Monat erstellt. Zu Beginn unterstützen wir Dich gerne dabei. Du benötigst ein Eurokonto, da wir in Euro auf das von Dir angegebene Konto überweisen. Es dauert nach unseren Erfahrungen in der Regel 2 bis 3 Tage, bis das Geld nach erfolgter Abrechnung auf Deinem Konto verbucht wird. Das Geld ist in der Regel zwischen dem 7. und 10. eines Monats auf dem Konto.

Wie läuft der Bewerbungsprozess?
Wenn Du Interesse hast, bei uns zu arbeiten, antworte einfach auf diese E-Mail oder kontaktiere und über den oben angegebenen Microsoft Teams Account. Wir sind auch später in unseren Projekt-Gruppen über Microsoft Teams organisiert und können uns hier den ganzen Tag untereinander austauschen.
Nachdem wir bei Microsoft Teams verbunden sind oder Du uns auf diese E-Mail geantwortet hast, laden wir Dich zu einem „Infomeeting“ ein, bei dem wir Dir das Projekt und die genauen Konditionen vorstellen und Du natürlich Deine Fragen loswerden kannst. Nach dem Infogespräch entscheiden wir gemeinsam, ob und wie es weitergehen wird.

CLINICAL DIRECTOR

Department: Anti-Trafficking

JOB SUMMARY

The Clinical Director provides clinical oversight to all aspects of clinical services provided by the One More Child Clinicians.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS

  • Provide clinical oversight to all clinicians and direct oversight to assigned clinicians.
  • Assist with the expansion of clinical/behavioral health services throughout all program areas as well as throughout the United States.
  • Assume responsibility for ensuring all clinical services billed are in alignment with Medicaid/insurance requirements.
  • Ensure clinical procedures/policies and practices align with COA and Medicaid requirements.
  • Complete/approve documentation as required by funding entities, courts, and referral sources .
  • Ensure the delivery of all aspects of clinical services including clinical quality management, and implementation of evidence-based treatments, testing/assessment, clinical outcomes initiatives, compliance with funding entities and other regulatory requirements.
  • Support clinicians in crisis intervention care in the immediate needs of victims as needed.
  • Assist Clinicians in assessing clients and developing/implementing individual clinical treatment plans and providing oversight as to progress and goal attainment of clinical treatment plans.
  • Provide unlicensed clinicians with the clinical supervision required for licensure (in alignment with applicable state laws/guidelines/requirements).
  • Participate in multidisciplinary teams to present cases for proper treatment.
  • Facilitate training for Clinicians and other OMC staff to ensure clients are receiving trauma-informed services.
  • Provide consultation to clinical staff and guidance in implementing evidence-based modalities including but not limited to TF-CBT, DBT, CT, Motivational Interviewing, and EMDR.
  • Stay current on emerging research in best practices and evidence-based practices specifically in serving populations who have experienced complex trauma and commercial sexual exploitation.
  • Collaborate with the other OMC Program Executive Directors to coordinate clinical services within the different program areas and to facilitate a positive and collaborative working environment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • N/A


REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s level degree in Social Work, Counseling Psychology, or a master’s degree with a concentration in one of the areas of Counseling such as: Mental Health Counseling, Clinical Mental Health Counseling.
  • Experience with clients who have experienced complex trauma including sexual abuse and/ or sexual exploitation.
  • Experience supervising clinical staff.
  • Florida licensure as LCSW/LICSW, LMHC, or LMFT.
  • Qualified Supervisor in the state of Florida for registered interns seeking licensure as clinical social workers, mental health counselors, and marriage and family therapists.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Licensure as LCSW/LICSW, LMHC, LMFT, LPC in the states of North Carolina, Tennessee, Ohio and Texas (or willingness to obtain within the first year of employment)
  • Florida Medicaid Provider Number (or willingness to obtain)
  • NPI / CAQH Number (or willingness to obtain)
  • Comprehensive understanding and experience in providing direct care and coordinated services to trauma victims specific to CSEC and CSE young adults.

  • Comprehensive understanding and experience in providing direct care and coordinated services to trauma victims.
  • Ability to build effective professional working relationships internally and externally.
  • Effective communication skills, both oral and written.
  • Presents him or herself outside the agency in a manner in keeping with the firm’s core values and guiding principles.

  • Computer and systems skills including experience with Microsoft Word.
  • Ability to build effective professional working relationships internally and externally.
  • Effective communication skills, both oral and written; attention to detail, and ability to multi–task and stay organized under tight deadlines.
  • Ability to protect the confidentiality of sensitive information.
  • Ability to understand and follow oral and written instructions, meets deadlines, and work independently.
  • Skills in effectively organizing work, files, records, etc., to maintain efficient workflow.
  • Ability to work effectively in a team, sharing tasks as necessary, both as a team leader and as a team member.
  • Availability to work flexible hours and days based on needs of the victims/survivors, ability to provide on-call services with team members for 24/7 and 365 days a year and provide crisis intervention and ongoing support of individuals identified in the region.
  • Team Player: ability to work effectively in a team, sharing tasks as necessary, both as a team leader and as a team member.
  • Computer and systems skills including experience with Microsoft Word.
  • Ability to solve complex, practical problems and effectively deal with complex variables in situations where limited standardization exists.

COMPETENCIES

  • Present oneself, both at and outside of work, in a manner keeping with One More Child’s Core Values of Humble, Hungry, Wise, and Called.
  • Ability to provide services with low barriers to clients within the community, including in clients’ homes.

Job Description

Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, Americas

Reports to the Head of Americas, Talent Acquisition

About Agilent

As a global leader in laboratory and clinical technologies, we are passionate about bringing great science to life. Our commitment to quality and innovation supports cutting-edge life science research, patient diagnostics, and ensures the safety of water, food, and pharmaceuticals. As scientists and clinicians pursue small, everyday advances and life-changing discoveries, we provide trusted answers to their most critical questions and challenges.

Leveraging more than 50 years of expertise, we create advanced instruments, software, and consumables supported by teams of highly skilled and knowledgeable people. With 18,000 employees around the world, our global reach and comprehensive solutions provide the most reliable and accurate results, as well as optimal scientific, economic, and operational outcomes. We work collaboratively with our customers on their journey to make a real difference in human lives. Our culture is founded on trust, respect, and uncompromising integrity, and we pride ourselves on being a dynamic and inclusive workplace that celebrates diversity and fosters innovation.

We can’t wait for you to join us as we continue our mission to improve the world around us. Information about Agilent is available at Agilent.com.

The Role

The Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, Americas plays a pivotal role in shaping the organization's future by identifying, attracting, and hiring top talent. This individual will partner closely with hiring managers and HR leaders across the organization to understand business objectives and develop recruitment strategies that align with the company's mission and strategic priorities.

As Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, Americas, this leader will serve as the Americas TA point of contact for one of our functions/businesses: Commercial, Operations, Enabling Functions, Technology, or Business Groups. This individual will partner closely with the aligned HRBP and hiring managers to conduct req activity oversight, execution of select reqs as part of a pod structure of TA delivery, and demonstrate active communication, reporting, and cross collaboration to achieve candidate, hiring manager, and stakeholder experience excellence.

As a trusted advisor, the Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, Americas will bring forward an ownership mentality, strategic insights, process excellence, and TA Advisory orientation as a business partner – demonstrating depth of knowledge of a customer base, talent market, and insights related to the respective business or function. The Lead Talent Acquisition Partner will executive full-cycle

recruitments, from sourcing and screening candidates to extending offers and ensuring a best-in class candidate experience. As part of a team/pod, the Lead Talent Acquisition Partner will work to develop robust talent pipelines and leverage data-driven insights to optimize hiring outcomes. This is an opportunity to make a significant impact and join a TA team and organization at a time of transformation and growth.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver end-to-end recruitment services while managing key hiring metrics.

  • Build and maintain strong consultative partnerships with hiring managers, HR partners, and business stakeholders.

  • Stay informed on business trends, labor market insights, and competitive talent intelligence.

  • Share market and candidate insights to influence hiring strategies through data and storytelling.

  • Develop and maintain a strong network of candidates and referral sources across corporate and operations talent pools.

  • Utilize technology and AI-enabled tools to efficiently identify, engage, and assess talent.

  • Collaborate with the broader Americas TA and Global TA teams to design and execute recruitment strategies aligned with business priorities.

  • Partner with peers to ensure consistent, compliant, and scalable hiring practices across the organization.

  • Research, design, and implement tailored recruitment strategies for newly assigned requisitions.

  • Champion a continuous improvement mindset by leveraging metrics, feedback, and best practices to evolve hiring strategies and optimize processes.

  • Experience recruiting across a range of disciplines and levels

  • Proven ability to act as a trusted advisor, influencing and partnering with leaders at all levels, including executives, through strong consultative communication.

  • Demonstrated experience working cross collaboratively with and ownership mentality

  • Excellent sourcing, networking, and market research skills.

  • Strong data-driven decision-making skills with experience analyzing trends and refining recruiting strategies.

  • Proficiency with applicant tracking systems and AI-driven technology

  • Nice to have: experience in life sciences, diagnostics, analytical instrumentation, medical technology or another regulated, science-driven industry.

  • Provides effective, practical advice to hiring managers, HR business partners, candidates, and other stakeholders involved in collective recruiting efforts

  • Action-oriented, with proven ability to lead key initiatives, motivate teams and drive decisions to closure.

jobs.description:
Become a part of our caring community

Associate Vice President, Conversational Channels

Position Summary

The Associate Vice President, Conversational Channels is a senior enterprise leader responsible for the experience across both sides of the member phone interaction—from intent identification, authentication, and routing to the tools, context, and workflows that enable advocates to resolve member needs.

The portfolio includes IVR, queuing and routing, AI-enabled customer engagement, Intelligent Search, Virtual Assistant, co-browse, and Customer Care Advocate CRM. This leader owns the product strategy, roadmap, experience design, and delivery of these capabilities, shaping an integrated experience that reduces friction and improves member outcomes and advocate effectiveness.

In partnership with contact center operations, technology, analytics, and Consumer Digital, this leader translates advocate feedback and operational priorities into sequenced investments that deliver measurable improvements in experience, service performance, efficiency, and business value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the conversational channel and advocate experience portfolio, including IVR, queuing and routing, AI-enabled customer engagement, Intelligent Search, Virtual Assistant, co-browse, and Customer Care Advocate CRM capabilities
  • Lead an integrated conversational engagement ecosystem across business segments, connecting member and advocate channels and touchpoints
  • Deliver seamless, AI-enabled experiences across the end-to-end member and advocate journey
  • Partner with Consumer Digital product leaders to create interconnected experiences between conversational channels and digital self-service, enabling seamless transitions, preserving member intent and context, and reducing the need for members to repeat information when moving between channels
  • Define and execute the multi-year strategy for the contact center advocate experience, translating advocate needs and operational insights into an integrated product roadmap that reduces friction, improves decision support, and enables more effective member interactions
  • Own product roadmaps and backlog prioritization, sequencing investments against the priority outcomes established with Client Services and making trade-off decisions when experience needs, platform constraints, and delivery capacity conflict
  • Establish and track outcomes for member experience, advocate productivity, authentication, misroutes, service quality, and enterprise transformation goals
  • Develop and execute multi-year product strategies aligned with Insurance and CenterWell segment business objectives
  • Lead the UX and interaction design of advocate capabilities across conversational channels, the advocate desktop, and digital capabilities invoked during advocate-assisted interactions, translating advocate feedback into intuitive, integrated experiences
  • Direct technical architecture, integration, release sequencing, and delivery quality across the advocate experience portfolio while partnering with Client Services on target workflows, service standards, training, and adoption
  • Establish and maintain product roadmaps that connect enterprise priorities to member and advocate experiences.
  • Evaluate market trends, member and advocate needs, competitive dynamics, and emerging technologies to inform strategic investments.
  • Lead a portfolio of products and platforms supporting IVR migration and modernization, conversational AI, Virtual Assistant, co-browse, Intelligent Search, and the advocate experience.
  • Apply deep knowledge of insurance and customer service to shape the responsible use of AI across advocate tools and member conversational channels
  • Ensure investments are prioritized based on business value, customer outcomes, regulatory requirements, and technical sustainability.
  • Balance enhancement of existing capabilities with innovation and modernization initiatives
  • Drive improvements in member and advocate experience through simplified, personalized, and connected interactions.


Use your skills to make an impact

Candidate Profile

Leadership Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in product management, conversational channels, contact center technology, customer experience, or platform strategy.
  • Deep expertise in contact center optimization, IVR, conversational AI, CRM platforms, advocate desktop capabilities, and enterprise AI enablement.
  • Experience leading products and platforms within Salesforce, Genesys, and Google Customer Engagement Suite (GECX), or comparable enterprise CRM and contact center technology ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated success leading large-scale, enterprise product portfolios and modernization initiatives within highly matrixed and regulated organizations.
  • Experience managing multiple product lines, leading director-level talent, and directing cross-functional teams across product, design, technology, analytics, and operations.
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to connect member and advocate experience, service performance, operational efficiency, and financial outcomes.
  • Proven ability to set multi-year strategy, manage outcome-based roadmaps and backlogs, prioritize investments, and make trade-off decisions across business value, experience needs, regulatory requirements, platform constraints, and delivery capacity.
  • Experience leading through influence across complex stakeholder environments and establishing clear decision rights, accountability, and escalation paths.
  • Demonstrated experience leading within a product operating model, including durable, cross-functional product teams, clear decision rights, outcome-based roadmaps, backlog prioritization, and continuous discovery and delivery.
  • Experience connecting conversational channels with digital self-service and advocate-assisted interactions, preserving member intent and context across channel transitions.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with contact center operational leaders to co-create the advocate experience vision and translate it into conversational channel strategy, product roadmaps, experience design, and delivered capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to use analytics, advocate feedback, service metrics, and human-centered design to shape experience priorities and measure improvements in member outcomes, advocate productivity, authentication, routing accuracy, service quality, and efficiency.

In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information.Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana's offices for training or meetings may be required.

40

jobs.excerpt: Le groupe juridique de Harris est à la recherche d’un(e) avocat(e) motivé(e), débrouillard(e), ayant un excellent sens des affaires, pour se joindre à notre équipe juridique!
jobs.description:
Le groupe juridique de Harris est à la recherche d’un(e) avocat(e) motivé(e), débrouillard(e), ayant un excellent sens des affaires, pour se joindre à notre équipe juridique!

Harris fait partie du groupe d’exploitation Harris de Constellation Software Inc., une société cotée à la Bourse de Toronto.

À titre de conseiller(ère) juridique commercial junior au Québec, vous vous concentrerez principalement sur l’examen des documents relatifs aux réponses aux appels d’offres de clients potentiels, la rédaction et la révision de contrats commerciaux régis notamment par le droit québécois, la négociation directe de contrats avec des tiers au nom de Harris ainsi que la formulation d’avis sur des questions liées à la protection des renseignements personnels au Québec et à l’intelligence artificielle.

La personne retenue relèvera du conseiller juridique principal – Affaires commerciales de Harris et aura l’occasion de contribuer à une grande variété de dossiers afin de soutenir l’ensemble du service juridique, sous la supervision du conseiller juridique principal – Affaires commerciales.

Ce poste exige une personne hautement organisée, dotée d’un excellent sens des affaires, d’un solide jugement commercial et de compétences exceptionnelles en rédaction juridique en français et en anglais. Le poste est basé au Québec, selon les modalités de travail applicables de Harris.

Votre rôle :

  • Prendre en charge les questions juridiques qui vous sont confiées par le conseiller juridique principal – Affaires commerciales.

  • Rédiger, examiner et négocier, en français et en anglais, un large éventail d’ententes et de contrats commerciaux avec des clients et des fournisseurs, notamment des contrats de licence, des ententes de revente, des ententes de services, des ententes de développement technologique et des ententes de confidentialité.

  • Selon votre niveau d’expérience, diriger, du début à la fin, la structuration, la rédaction, l’examen, la négociation et la conclusion de transactions commerciales et corporatives.

  • Créer et tenir à jour des modèles d’ententes en français et en anglais en fonction des exigences commerciales et juridiques applicables au Québec.

  • Collaborer étroitement avec les autres membres du service juridique et de conformité ainsi qu’avec les équipes interfonctionnelles de Harris afin de cerner les besoins, de fournir des conseils aux clients internes et de soutenir la croissance des activités de Harris.

  • Représenter les besoins et les préoccupations des unités d’affaires de Harris dans les interactions avec les clients, les fournisseurs et les autres partenaires; collaborer avec des conseillers juridiques externes dans le cadre de négociations et du règlement de différends.

  • Surveiller et cerner de manière proactive les tendances et les risques juridiques découlant de l’évolution de l’environnement législatif et réglementaire québécois et fédéral, notamment en droit commercial, en protection des renseignements personnels, en cybersécurité et en langue française.

  • Participer à l’élaboration et à l’amélioration des programmes de conformité pertinents afin d’assurer le respect des règles québécoises en matière de contrats des organismes publics ainsi que des lois canadiennes et québécoises relatives à la protection des renseignements personnels, notamment la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels dans le secteur privé et les exigences issues de la Loi 25.

Qualifications :

  • Baccalauréat en droit civil (LL.B. ou équivalent) d’une faculté de droit reconnue.

  • Admission au Barreau du Québec et statut de membre en règle, avec droit d’exercice au Québec.

  • De 0 à 3 ans d’expérience en droit commercial ou des technologies au Québec, au sein d’un cabinet reconnu ou à titre de conseiller(ère) juridique en entreprise.

  • Capacité à travailler de façon autonome avec les unités d’affaires et à accomplir ses tâches de manière indépendante.

  • Excellentes compétences en gestion du temps et capacité à gérer simultanément plusieurs échéances et priorités.

  • Capacité à analyser des situations et des données complexes afin d’évaluer les risques, les répercussions et les prochaines étapes, ainsi qu’à faire preuve de curiosité et de créativité pour résoudre des enjeux variés.

  • Aptitude à bien travailler avec les autres et intérêt à faire partie d’une équipe juridique soudée.

  • Connaissance des solutions SaaS, hébergement, des contrats de licence de logiciels et du droit des obligations et des contrats en droit québécois.

  • Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral et à l’écrit, afin de rédiger et de négocier des contrats et de conseiller des unités d’affaires et des partenaires au Québec et ailleurs au Canada; connaissance de la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels dans le secteur privé, de la Loi 25 et des lois fédérales applicables en matière de protection des renseignements personnels.

Égalité d’accès à l’emploi

Toutes les personnes qualifiées seront considérées pour un emploi sans égard à leur race, leur couleur, leur sexe, leur identité ou expression de genre, leur grossesse, leur orientation sexuelle, leur état civil, leur âge sauf dans la mesure prévue par la loi, leur religion, leurs convictions politiques, leur langue, leur origine ethnique ou nationale, leur condition sociale, leur handicap ou l’utilisation d’un moyen pour pallier ce handicap, ou toute autre caractéristique protégée par les lois applicables au Québec.

The Harris Legal Group is seeking a business-oriented, motivated, resourceful Québec lawyer to join our Legal Team! Harris is part of the Harris Operating Group of Constellation Software Inc. which is publicly listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. As a Junior Commercial Counsel in Québec, you will be primarily focused on reviewing potential customer Request for Proposal Documents; drafting and reviewing commercial contracts governed in particular by Québec law, negotiating contracts directly with third parties on behalf of Harris, providing opinions on Québec privacy issues and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will report to Harris’ Commercial Senior Counsel and will have a wide variety of options to choose from to assist the entire legal department through the Commercial General Counsel and other Senior Counsel’s oversight.

This role requires a highly business oriented and organized individual with strong business judgment and exceptional French and English drafting skills. The position is based in Québec, subject to Harris’ applicable work arrangements.

What your role will be:

  • Responsible for legal matters for assigned by the commercial senior counsel.

  • Draft, review and negotiate, in French and English, a wide range of commercial agreements and contracts for customers and vendors, including license agreements, reseller agreements, service agreements, technology development agreements, and non-disclosure agreements.

  • Based on experience level, lead, from beginning to end, the structuring, drafting, reviewing, negotiating and closing of corporate and commercial transactions.

  • Create and maintain French and English template agreements based on business and legal requirements applicable in Québec.

  • Work closely with the other members of the Legal & Compliance Department and cross-functional teams across Harris to identify needs, advise and counsel internal clients, and support Harris’ business growth.

  • Represent the needs and concerns of Harris business units when interacting with customers, vendors and other partners; interact with external counsel on negotiations and dispute resolution.

  • Review and proactively identify legal trends and risks arising from the changing Québec and federal legislative and regulatory environment, including commercial law, privacy, cybersecurity and French-language requirements.

  • Assist in developing and improving relevant compliance programs to ensure adherence to Québec public-sector contracting requirements and Canadian and Québec privacy laws, including the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector and the requirements introduced by Law 25.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil law (LL.B. or equivalent) from an accredited law school.

  • Admission to the Barreau du Québec, membership in good standing and authorization to practise law in Québec.

  • 0 – 3 years of experience in commercial or technology law in Québec with a well-respected firm or as in-house counsel.

  • Ability to work autonomously with business units and independently.

  • Excellent time management skills and the ability to handle multiple time constraints with various priorities.

  • Able to analyze complex situations and data to determine risks, impact, and next steps; and to use curiosity and creativity to solve diverse issues.

  • Working well with others and enjoying being part of a cohesive legal team.

  • Familiarity with SaaS, Cloud, software license agreements, and the law of obligations and contracts under Québec law.

  • Excellent oral and written proficiency in French and English, to draft and negotiate agreements and advise business units and partners in Québec and elsewhere in Canada; knowledge of the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, Law 25 and applicable federal privacy legislation.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to the individual’s race, color, sex, national origin, religion, age, disability, genetic information, status as a military veteran, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Position Overview

MetroSys is seeking an experienced Senior SCCM Patch Management Consultant to support a regional credit union in assessing, improving, and modernizing its enterprise patch-management environment.

The consultant will serve as a subject matter expert for Microsoft SCCM / Microsoft Configuration Manager, reviewing the client's current SCCM architecture, patching processes, deployment methodology, reporting, automation, and overall patch compliance.

This role will begin with a comprehensive assessment of the existing environment and progress into recommendations and hands-on improvements. The consultant will identify SCCM configuration gaps, improve patching processes, increase automation, and help establish a more reliable and repeatable enterprise patch-management program.

The environment is primarily Microsoft-based with some Linux infrastructure and supports banking, security, and regulated workloads. The consultant should understand the operational and compliance requirements associated with patching systems within a financial-services environment.

The initial engagement is expected to last approximately three months, with the possibility of extension and/or permanent employment based on project needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform a comprehensive assessment of the existing SCCM / Microsoft Configuration Manager environment and enterprise patch-management process.
  • Review SCCM architecture, site configuration, distribution points, Software Update Points, WSUS integration, client health, boundaries, collections, and overall platform health.
  • Evaluate existing SCCM Software Update Groups, Automatic Deployment Rules (ADRs), device collections, maintenance windows, deployment schedules, and reboot policies.
  • Review current Windows Server and endpoint patching processes to identify coverage gaps, failed deployments, configuration issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Assess SCCM patch-compliance reporting and develop recommendations for improving visibility into compliant, non-compliant, failed, offline, and pending-reboot systems.
  • Design or improve SCCM patching rings and deployment collections for test, pilot, production, critical infrastructure, and exception groups.
  • Develop and implement SCCM automation to reduce manual patch-management activities and improve consistency.
  • Utilize PowerShell and other automation technologies to improve SCCM administration, reporting, remediation, and patching workflows.
  • Review existing patch testing, approval, deployment, rollback, maintenance-window, and emergency patching procedures.
  • Identify opportunities to automate patch identification, deployment, validation, remediation, and compliance reporting.
  • Evaluate where AI-assisted technologies could provide practical value within patch management, reporting, troubleshooting, vulnerability prioritization, or operational workflows.
  • Work with security and vulnerability-management teams to align SCCM patch deployments with identified vulnerabilities and organizational risk.
  • Support patching requirements across a primarily Microsoft environment, while helping establish appropriate processes for Linux and other infrastructure not directly managed through SCCM.
  • Review patch-management practices against applicable banking, security, PCI, and internal compliance requirements.
  • Troubleshoot SCCM client, deployment, distribution, update, and reporting issues.
  • Create or improve patch-management dashboards, reports, KPIs, and audit documentation.
  • Develop a prioritized SCCM and patch-management improvement roadmap.
  • Implement approved SCCM configuration, automation, reporting, and process improvements during the engagement.
  • Document configurations, procedures, recommendations, and operational standards and provide knowledge transfer to internal teams.

Job Description:

The Senior Product Manager, Clinical Content owns the product strategy, roadmap, and delivery for one or more product areas within the Clinical Content portfolio. This individual applies strong product management fundamentals — discovery, prioritization, experimentation, and measurable KPIs — to define and execute a roadmap that maximizes customer value and business results. The Senior Product Manager partners closely with engineering, design, data, and go-to-market teams to bring the roadmap to life, and serves as a subject-matter expert and mentor to other product managers, contributing to the company's broader effort to modernize and scale the product management function around strong technology product management craft. For this role, the portfolio is the company's ambulatory EHR and practice management platform, spanning the clinical documentation, ordering, e-prescribing, scheduling, patient access, and revenue cycle workflows that physician practices and ambulatory organizations depend on daily; the Senior Product Manager therefore pairs strong product craft with domain fluency in ambulatory care delivery and healthcare interoperability.
  • Own the product roadmap and backlog for one or more [Clinical Content product areas, from discovery through launch and post-launch iteration.
  • Contribute to and help execute the product-led growth (PLG) strategy for the product portfolio, identifying opportunities to expand adoption and usage through the product experience.
  • Partner closely with engineering, design, and data teams to define and execute the roadmap and backlog, applying strong product management fundamentals (discovery, prioritization, experimentation, and measurable KPIs) to deliver an exceptional end-to-end user experience.
  • Write clear product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria, and work with the VP/Director of Product Management and executive leadership to inform the broader strategic plan for business growth, including new product development and build-vs-buy-vs-partner input.
  • Maintain a deep, current understanding of prospects, customers, competitors, and partners (their strategic direction, pain points, desired integrations, and buying behavior) to inform product decisions, market positioning, and competitive differentiation.
  • Define and track the product metrics that define success for the product area (activation, adoption, expansion revenue, retention, churn, and customer/patient satisfaction) and use them to drive continuous improvement.
  • Coordinate product releases to ensure alignment between product, support, and service operations, and partner with finance, sales, and product marketing on go-to-market messaging, pricing input, and business models that support both sales-assisted and product-led paths to revenue.
  • Support business and contractual discussions with partners specific to the market, as needed.
  • Ensure regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to the product line are identified, accurate, and delivered within deadlines, partnering with legal, compliance, and regulatory affairs as needed.
  • Establish and maintain a robust product lifecycle management framework, focused on modernizing aged products and building toward a scalable, extensible technology and platform architecture.
  • Contribute to forecasting and reporting on revenue, cost, and margin for the product area, and bring the discipline and rigor of sound business judgment to product decisions.
  • Mentor and provide guidance to Product Managers and Associate Product Managers on strong product management craft (discovery, prioritization, roadmapping, execution), helping them deliver high-quality products within aggressive timelines regardless of subject matter.
  • Perform other duties that support the overall objective of the position.

Education Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in business, computer science, biology, engineering, or a related field.
  • An MBA, MHA or other advanced business degree is a plus.
  • Or, any combination of education and experience which would provide the required qualifications for the position.

Experience Required:

  • 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in technology/software product management, with a proven ability to own and deliver results for ambulatory EHR and practice management product areas.
  • Direct experience owning or contributing to ambulatory EHR and practice management products, with deep familiarity across the clinical and front/back-office workflows they support, including provider documentation, computerized order entry, e-prescribing (eRx/EPCS), clinical decision support, patient scheduling and registration, eligibility, and end-to-end revenue cycle management.
  • Healthcare/healthcare IT industry experience, ideally in an Ambulatory or Acute Healthcare environment, is preferred but secondary to demonstrated product management skill.
  • Ambulatory clinical and practice-management workflows, including provider documentation, computerized order entry, e-prescribing, clinical decision support, patient scheduling and access, eligibility, and end-to-end revenue cycle management (charge capture, coding, claims, and patient collections). Experience with ambulatory regulatory and quality programs, including ONC Health IT Certification (CEHRT), CMS incentive and quality programs (MIPS/MACRA and Promoting Interoperability), clinical quality measurement (eCQMs), information-blocking compliance, and value-based care and patient-engagement capabilities.
  • Experience contributing to the definition, launch, and scaling of AI/ML-powered product capabilities (for example, clinical decision support, predictive and risk analytics, ambient/automated documentation, and generative AI/LLM features), with attention to model performance, clinical validation, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience partnering with data science and engineering teams to operationalize AI/ML across the model lifecycle (data strategy, model development and evaluation, and production monitoring), including build-vs-buy decisions across foundation models, third-party vendors, and in-house capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability owning a significant product area with clear business impact, including exposure to revenue, cost, and margin considerations, and a track record of bringing complex, multi-stakeholder solutions to market.
  • Experience contributing to product-led growth motions (e.g., free trial/freemium, self-serve onboarding, in-product upsell and expansion, usage-based pricing) in a B2B SaaS or technology environment.
  • Experience writing business cases, performing market analysis, contributing to go-to-market strategy, and managing backlogs and pricing/packaging input across multiple markets.
  • Experience navigating complex, ambiguous business situations and managing multiple stakeholders with diverse priorities (including finance, sales, and engineering) to achieve consensus and drive results.
  • Experience in a private equity-owned company preferred, especially in a growth-focused environment.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

Knowledge of:

  • General technology product management best practices, product-led growth strategy and metrics, SaaS business models and unit economics, and general business acumen.
  • Minimum Viable Product (MVP) concept and Agile development process; Product Lifecycle practices.
  • Deep understanding of healthcare technology and a passion for improving patient and provider experiences
  • AI and generative AI product fundamentals, including the model lifecycle (data, training, evaluation, and monitoring/MLOps), large language models, and how to translate AI capabilities into differentiated, defensible product value.
  • Responsible and trustworthy AI in healthcare, including bias mitigation, transparency and explainability, human-in-the-loop design, data privacy and security (HIPAA), and the evolving regulatory landscape for AI-enabled products

Skill in:

  • Leadership through influence, financial and business acumen, communication, cross-functional collaboration, executive-level presentation, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

Ability to:

  • Define and manage complex processes, workflows, and product issues;
  • Develop compelling product vision and drive it to successful execution;
  • Contribute to the design and scaling of product-led growth motions
  • Collaborate with and mentor a team of global professionals in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment;
  • Manage a product area with strong business rigor and discipline
  • Work on concurrent projects with critical/urgent timelines;
  • Disseminate product concepts, updates, and deliverables;
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships through collaboration and respect.

  • A Consultant’s Rolodex: You don’t rely solely on cold calls. You have deep-rooted, trust-based relationships with PBM/Health Plan Executive, clinicians and consultants who will open doors for you on day one.

An Associate’s Degree or Bachelor’s Degree is preferred.

JOB RELEVANT EXPERIENCE:

  • Deep Rolodex: An active, established network of national and regional benefits consultants and brokers (e.g., Mercer, WTW, Aon, Lockton).
  • Subject Matter Mastery: Understanding of PBM mechanics, including formulary management, clinical programs, specialty pharmacy, pricing models, and rebate structures.
  • Executive Presence: Exceptional communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to command a room during finalist meetings.

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Any lifting, bending, traveling, etc. required to do the job duties listed above. Long periods of sitting and computer work.

WORK FROM HOME TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Supply and support their own internet services.

Maintaining an uninterrupted internet connection is a requirement of all work from home positions.

Join our team at Dane Street and enjoy a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and peace of mind. We offer a range of benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family. Additionally, we offer voluntary life insurance options for you, your spouse, and your children. We also offer other voluntary benefits which include hospital indemnity, critical illness, accident indemnity, and pet insurance plans. Employees receive basic life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage at no cost. Our generous paid time off policy ensures you have time to relax and recharge, while our 401k plan with a company match helps you plan for your future. Apple equipment and a media stipend are provided for remote workspace.

A fast-paced, Inc. 500 Company with a high-performance culture, is seeking insightful forward-thinking professionals. jobs.excerpt: About PlasmaPlasma is building the primary account for global money.
jobs.description:
About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

The Context

The design team at Plasma is small by choice. Two senior designers currently cover the whole of Plasma One, from core money movement flows through to the design system. You would be the third.

Design is a first-class input here. It shapes product direction, technical tradeoffs, and whether people trust us with their money.

You would help decide how design actually works: how decisions get made, how work is reviewed, how quality holds up under speed, and how a coherent system takes shape as the product grows. There is no process to inherit and no large team to hide inside. What you build becomes the standard.

The team works closely with engineering and the growth team. Designers at Plasma are expected to think in systems, understand real constraints, and push for clarity where ambiguity is expensive. The bar is high, feedback is direct, and the impact is visible quickly.

This suits someone who wants autonomy and responsibility, who wants to build the product that changes how money moves, and the team behind it.

The Work

  • Own the Plasma experience. Invent new features and shape how Plasma One feels to use, taking ideas from concept to launch. Turn the advantages of stablecoins and blockchain into experiences that make people’s financial lives better.

  • Extend your abilities with AI. Use AI as a core tool to explore more ambitious ideas, build functional prototypes, and push what you can design and deliver.

  • Bring ideas to life. Turn abstract concepts into working coded prototypes, then collaborate with engineers who share your attention to detail to bring them into production. Refine microinteractions, motion, and visual polish together.

  • Evolve the design system. Build reusable components and interaction patterns that keep the product coherent as it grows, with design and implementation aligned.

  • Learn from real use. Combine research, usability testing, and product data to discover opportunities and improve what you ship.



The Bar

  • Substantial consumer product experience. Typically 6+ years in product design, including shipped native iOS and/or Android work and meaningful contributions to a design system.

  • A portfolio with exceptional craft. Show us the details you refined, the reasoning behind them, and your contribution to the finished product. We want to understand your taste and how you decide when an experience is ready.

  • Confidence with functional prototyping. You can make an idea tangible enough to test its behaviour and communicate the intended experience to engineers. Understanding or writing code is a bonus, not a requirement.

  • Sound product judgment. You can explain how user evidence changed a decision, what you chose to prioritise, and what happened after launch. You are comfortable making progress when the brief is incomplete.

  • Direct, thoughtful collaboration. You make your reasoning easy to follow, give specific feedback, and can disagree constructively. You know when to work independently and when to bring others into a decision.

What's in it for you

  • Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

  • A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

  • Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

  • Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

  • All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

  • Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

jobs.description:
This is a remote role. CircleLink Health is looking for passionate, tech savvy registered nurses to work remotely and serve patients enrolled in Medicare’s Chronic Care Management Program. In this part time role (about 20-25 hrs. per week), an RN Care Coach will be assigned a group of patients that they will be following and calling each month. In these monthly calls you will provide education, coordinate care, close preventive care gaps, and coach on strategies for self-management to keep them out of the hospital.

This Role Requires Precision, Discipline, and Accountability

The Care Manager role is not a step back from bedside nursing — it’s a step into a more complex, structured, and performance-driven environment. To succeed, you must bring more than clinical knowledge:

✅ Excellent documentation skills — Your charting must be complete, timely, and accurate.

✅ Strong time management — Case tasks must be prioritized and closed on schedule.

✅ Ownership of outcomes — Each case is closely tracked for quality, compliance, and effectiveness.

Expectations are high, and performance is regularly reviewed. This is not a role where details can be missed or timelines pushed — we need professionals who take initiative, stay organized, and consistently deliver.

If you’re ready for a challenging, fast-paced environment where your work is held to high standards and makes a real difference, we encourage you to apply.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Utilize our specialized care management software to call Medicare patients with 2 or more chronic conditions (Diabetes, CHF, Chronic Pain, COPD, etc.) on a monthly basis
  • Build and maintain rapport with patients to help coach them to improved health through SMART goals and education on self-management strategies
  • Implement and improve the Plan of Care by updating medications, appointments due, biometrics, symptoms, and interventions made
  • Connect the patient with community resources as needed, including transportation, personal care needs, prescription/DME assistance, social services, etc.
  • Conduct Transitional Care Management activities to high risk patients discharged from the hospital and the ER to reduce unnecessary readmissions.
  • Close care gaps by encouraging and assisting with preventive care measures, i.e. annual well visits, vaccines, cancer screens, follow-up/specialist appointments, etc.

Requirements

  • Fluent in English
  • Self-directed, able to work independently with little supervision while meeting performance metrics
  • Passion for nursing and improving patient outcomes
  • Good with technology and eager to learn and use new software
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills
  • Timely communication is essential, and nurses are expected to respond to all messages and emails within 24–48 hours.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

Education and Experience:

  • Current, unrestricted Compact License / multistate RN license
  • Proficiency with electronic health records and web-based applications
  • 3+ years' experience as a Registered Nurse

Preferred Education and Experience, but not required:

  • Spanish fluency
  • Case Management or Chronic Disease Management experience highly preferred
  • Certified Diabetes Educator
  • Experience with Motivational Interviewing or other behavior change communication techniques

Scheduling and Other Requirements

  • RN needs a STRONG internet-connected computer
  • Minimum of 20 hours of availability per week required
  • You will commit to your own schedule using our software.
  • This is a 1099 contract position with no end date. Care coaches are responsible for their own taxes and insurance.

Benefits

Compensation:

RN Care Coach compensation is paid at the rate of $15.00 for the first 20-minute increment (20-min milestone), $12 for the second 20-minute increment (40-min milestone), and$11.50 for the 3rd 20-minute increment (60-min milestone).

A clinical encounter occurs after two criteria are met: 1/ A successful interactive clinical call with the patient or their caregiver. 2/ A 20-min, or 40-min, or 60-min milestone is met on the patient's chart. Example pay scenarios, but not limited to:

  • Two 20-min successful calls with 2 different patients pays $30 for the two 20-min visits. ($15+$15=$30)
  • A 40-min encounter with the same patient pays $27. ($15+$12=$27).
  • A 60-min encounter with the same patient pays $38.50. ($15+$12+$11.50=$38.50)

Pay Timing:

Monthly via direct deposit, 40 days after the last day of the month of service. This is due to the time it takes Medicare to process reimbursements. Your pay after the first check will be 30 days from the end of the previous month.

Fraud Alert:

CircleLink Health has identified fraudulent emails sent from @joincirclelinkhealth.team, which is NOT affiliated with our company. Official CircleLink emails come only from @circlelinkhealth.com. Please report any suspicious messages to .

About CircleLink Health:

CircleLink Health is a company of passionate clinicians, technologists and businesspeople tackling the $600B problem of preventable chronic and post-acute complications. We’re building a world-class Care Management platform to enable providers while accelerating the shift to preventative care instead of status quo reactive care. Learn more about us here.
