jobs.title: Senior Manager, Research Management & Impact
jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Heart & Stroke our mission is to promote health, save lives and enhance recovery.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Heart & Stroke our mission is to promote health, save lives and enhance recovery. We are committed to a culture that exemplifies our core values: champion health, practice humility, embrace change, drive impact, learn and grow and be heartfelt as we work together to beat heart disease and stroke.

We believe in equity, diversity and inclusion ― it’s embedded in our values and core mission work to support all people in Canada to lead healthier lives. We are committed to applying this principle to cultivate a welcoming environment that embraces diversity among our employees. Candidates from diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to, Indigenous peoples, racialized communities, 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, women, and people living with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

To learn more about our mission, values, commitment to EDI, and the difference Heart & Stroke makes in the lives of people in Canada at every age, please visit our website.

The opportunity

Please note Heart & Stroke offers a hybrid work option, and candidates can work from anywhere in Canada. There is also occasional travel (including overnight) required up to 10 days/year.

We are currently looking for a Senior Manager, Research Management & Impact role to join our Research & Science team. Reporting to the Vice President, Research & Science, the role oversees the post funding management and impact of Heart & Stroke funded research. This role is accountable for leading the administration of Heart & Stroke’s funded research portfolio, including compliance, post-funding management, reporting, and processes that support the measurement, maximization, and communication of research impact.

A core part of the role is the administration, compliance, and oversight of Heart & Stroke’s funded research portfolio across the post-funding lifecycle. This includes ensuring that recipients and institutions meet funding requirements, overseeing payment and claims processes, supporting annual reporting, coordinating mid-point reviews, managing end-of-funding reporting, and identifying and escalating risks or issues that may affect accountability, stewardship, or compliance. The role also supports annual business planning, process improvement, and the modernization of research management and reporting systems to strengthen efficiency, data quality, and organizational insight.

The role will also lead the identification, interpretation, and communication of the impact of Heart & Stroke funded research. Working closely with the VP, Research & Science and cross-functional partners, the role develops approaches to capture, analyze, and translate research outcomes into meaningful insights, narratives, and evidence-informed recommendations. Through these approaches the role serves to support organizational strategy, knowledge mobilization, marketing, fundraising, advocacy, and mission priorities. Finally, the role serves as a key functional lead for research and science impact by supporting effective, integrated, and coordinated action that helps position the organization at the leading edge of evolving evidence and best practices in heart and brain health.

How you will make an impact every day

Annual business planning, implementation and coordination of Heart & Stroke funded grants and awards

  • Leads the annual planning process for post-award management and research impact, establishing priorities, deliverables, timelines, governance, and resource requirements aligned with organizational strategy.

  • Creates the knowledge translation and mobilization framework for Heart & Stroke research, ensuring it aligns with the Foundation’s impact goals and performance strategy.

  • Offers strategic leadership in the development and implementation of knowledge translation and mobilization initiatives for Heart & Stroke funded research.

  • Directs cross-functional planning and prioritization with input from mission leadership to identify key research and science impacts of Heart & Stroke programs.

  • Leads the identification, assessment, and interpretation of research and science impacts relevant to Heart & Stroke priorities, translating insights into recommendations for programs, strategy, and mission execution.

  • Advises senior leadership on risks, trade-offs, and opportunities related to research management and impact frameworks, practices, policies and procedures.

  • Leads organizational alignment of research and science impact work with mission strategy, ensuring a coordinated and consistent approach across functions, priorities, and audiences.

  • Establishes governance, decision-making, and escalation processes for post-award management and research impact work, balancing risk, capacity, and organizational priorities.

Post grant and award management and administration

  • Leads the post-award compliance function, ensuring grant holders and host institutions adhere to grant agreements, policies, and reporting requirements, and establishing risk-based approaches for monitoring and escalation.

  • Provides strategic leadership and subject-matter expertise to the SRC budget review process, including the refinement of budget review guidelines, adjudication standards, and stewardship expectations.

  • Oversees the integrity of post-award financial records and reporting, ensuring accurate tracking, reconciliation, and contribution to departmental financial planning and annual reporting.

  • Oversees post-award claims and payment processes, ensuring strong financial controls, policy adherence, stewardship of funds, and timely resolution of complex issues.

  • Exercises decision-making authority over non-routine post-award financial and compliance issues, assessing risk, determining appropriate resolution or escalation, and safeguarding organizational resources and reputation.

  • Partners with Finance to strengthen controls, forecasting, reporting, audit readiness, and stewardship practices related to funded research.

Business analysis and research information management

  • Leads the modernization of grant management, reporting, and knowledge translation systems, identifying and implementing improved processes, tools, and technologies that strengthen efficiency, data quality, and organizational insight.

  • Establishes organizational frameworks and standards for research program metrics and performance reporting, and synthesizes findings into actionable insights for senior leadership decision-making.

  • Leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of progress and final reporting mechanisms to strengthen evidence capture, compliance oversight, mission impact assessment, and organizational learning.

Translation of funded research results to support marketing and fundraising.

  • Leads enterprise-wide cross-functional approaches in collaboration with department specialists to translate funded research into impact narratives and stories that will support digital, marketing, communications and development.

  • Shapes the research and science content strategy in collaboration with the VP, Research and Science for fundraising and marketing campaigns by identifying timely, credible, and mission-relevant discoveries, milestones, and impact stories.

  • Contribute to fundraising and marketing campaigns e.g. year end, heart month, stroke month with relevant high-value research impact narratives, opportunity identification, and scientifically sound positioning of Heart & Stroke funded research.

  • Partners with Development leadership to inform, strategize and support fundraising plans to maximize the impact of Heart & Stroke research programs.

  • Synthesizes and interprets research impact data to inform fundraising, health information, public awareness, and stewardship priorities.

  • Leads and advises on the accurate, timely, and audience-appropriate dissemination of mission impact stories and research evidence across organizational channels (i.e., fundraising, development, marketing and communications teams).

  • Provide input on funded research content and data for donor proposals and pitches.

  • Serves as a key advisor to the VP, Research and Science and other leaders on research impact strategy.

Team Leadership

  • Provide clear direction, guidance and feedback on day-to-day activities and priorities.

  • Builds a high-performing, collaborative team culture that enables strong cross-functional partnership, accountability, and continuous improvement.

  • In partnership with the Vice President, Research and Science, establishes performance plan and objectives and review on an ongoing basis.

  • As required, recruit skilled talent in support of current and future Foundation needs, following Foundation policies, interviewing methodology and assessment guidelines.

  • Familiarize and comply with all Heart & Stroke policies while ensuring accurate administration of employee related information: absence records, vacation, title, etc.

Who we need

Education

  • Masters in science within a health research related field

  • Cerebrovascular and cardiovascular subject matter expertise is a strong asset.

  • Knowledge related to knowledge translation and mobilization frameworks, required.

  • Knowledge related to the Canadian health research system and health care delivery, required.

Experience

  • Minimum 7 years’ experience in a management role.

  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in research, with a preference for health research grant management and administration, including compliance, progress reporting, financial claims, and grant close-out.

  • Experience in analyzing and interpreting research and clinical data.

  • Experience managing operational budgets and external vendors/consultants (SOWs, contracts, deliverables, performance).

  • Experience in bringing together a range of constituents in pursuit of shared objectives, aligned to organizational values and policy position, including people with lived experience.

  • Experience in planning knowledge translation and mobilization frameworks to support evidence-informed health policy and practice.

  • Experience in a cross-functional role in an organization that crosses departments and seeks overall alignment.

  • Demonstrated experience implementing KT/KM initiatives (e.g., evidence-to-action products, convenings, practice/policy engagement, dissemination strategies) and measuring uptake.

  • Extensive knowledge of frameworks and tools required to promote and measure health equity, including anti-oppressive and anti-racist strategies,

  • Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous history, colonization, racism, and Calls to Action

  • Experience engaging external partners with a focus on building health equity within the cardiovascular and stroke health system in Canada.

Skills

  • Excellent leadership skills and ability to influence others by articulating sound, rational arguments.

  • Ability to establish, lead and maintain positive working relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, influencing teams within and outside your department.

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication and negotiation skills are essential. Strong writing skills are imperative.

  • Exercises sound judgment in ambiguous situations.

  • Ability to translate complex scientific information into practical organizational action.

  • Demonstrated leadership of enterprise cross-functional initiatives with governance, deliverables, timelines, and risk management.

  • Ability to develop trusting relationships and partnerships with diverse groups and co-create win-win solutions that advance the Foundation’s mission.

  • Excellent strategic thinking and change management skills

  • Excellent presentation, verbal and written communication skills to prepare wide range of outputs and help stakeholders understand data/evidence. Effective communicator both verbally and in written formats; capable of communicating technical content to audiences at varying levels of knowledge

  • Desire and ability to acquire technical knowledge of the scientific and research issues associated with heart disease and stroke

  • Ability to work inter-departmentally and to communicate effectively with senior volunteers and staff across the Foundation, providing guidance and supporting its application.

  • Strong computer skills and ability to use technological tools to organize and advance the work of the team (i.e., MS Office Suite, SharePoint, CRM and other workflow tools, digital engagement platforms).

  • An ability to work in both official languages is an asset.

What we offer

At Heart & Stroke, we make it a priority to foster a culture of caring by implementing practices and programs that foster respect, compassion, trust and attentiveness to our own and others’ health and well-being.

This role offers a hiring range of $95,000 to $119,000, aligned with our compensation framework and your professional background. We believe that time off is integral to the personal health and wellness of our employees. We offer a generous paid time-off package including vacation days, personal days, wellness days, and paid company-wide closure between December 25 and January 1. We also provide competitive health, medical, dental and vision benefits, life insurance, disability benefits, an employee assistance program (EAP) and a defined contribution pension plan with employer matching. Our employees also enjoy a flexible hybrid working model and reimbursement for mobile phones and home office setup, as well as opportunities for professional development.

Apply now

If you want to join the fight to beat heart disease and stroke, please apply by sending your resume by September 30,2026. Applicants must be currently residing in Canada and legally entitled to work in Canada.

Only those candidates that qualify will be selected for an interview. Interviews may be conducted virtually or in-person. Selected candidates will be notified in advance if an in-person interview is required.

Accommodation

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, barrier-free and accessible environment. If you have been contacted for an interview and require accommodation to participate in the recruitment and selection process, please let us know and we will do our best to address your needs.

jobs.title: Director, UI/UX Design
jobs.excerpt: Who we areAt WELLSTAR, we are committed to reshaping Canadian healthcare by leveraging technology to address the administrative burdens that pull physicians away from their true calling—patient care.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At WELLSTAR, we are committed to reshaping Canadian healthcare by leveraging technology to address the administrative burdens that pull physicians away from their true calling—patient care. Our mission is to support providers and patients, shifting the emphasis back to quality, timeliness, and positive outcomes. With a comprehensive suite of technology solutions, we have successfully helped thousands of providers adopt and benefit from modern, interoperable technologies that improve patient outcomes and system efficiency.

Whether you are in research and development, administration, communications, operations leadership, or technology, joining us now is an opportunity to play a critical role in transforming how healthcare is managed and experienced in Canada.

The opportunity

WELLSTAR, a majority-owned subsidiary of WELL Health Technologies Corp, is a high-growth SaaS company with a focused objective of reshaping healthcare through digital enablement. Our innovative solutions are designed to streamline care delivery, integrate healthcare systems and improve patient outcomes.

Reporting to the VP, Product Management, we are hiring a Director, UI/UX Design to lead the design function for the Clinical Platform Group. As our new Director, UI/UX Design, you will lead and develop an established team of designers while owning the quality, consistency, and evolution of the end-to-end product experience. You will set the design direction for a modern, AI-first EMR platform, strengthen user research and design practices, and ensure the needs of clinicians remain central to how the product evolves. Working as a peer to Product and Engineering leadership, you will bring greater structure and consistency to how teams collaborate from problem definition and discovery through design, development, and release.

This is a remote-first role open to candidates anywhere in Canada, with occasional travel for team on-sites and clinic visits.

What’s in it for you

Leadership and influence. You will step into an established design team with the opportunity to make a strong team even better. You will have the scope to develop designers, raise the bar on craft and consistency, and shape how the design function evolves as the product and organization grow. Working alongside Product and Engineering leadership, you will have a voice in decisions that influence both the product experience and how teams work together.

Shape an AI-first healthcare experience. You will help define how clinicians interact with AI in a product they rely on to deliver care. From how AI-generated suggestions are presented to how confidence, transparency, and clinician control are built into the experience, you will influence some of the most important design questions facing Nexus AI EMR as the platform evolves.

Build better ways of working. You will have the opportunity to strengthen and mature an existing design practice rather than build one from the ground up. You will refine research, design processes, cross-functional collaboration, and the design system, creating the structure that helps designers do their best work and enables Product, Design, and Engineering to move forward together.

What you will do:

  • Lead and develop the design team. You will coach and support an established team of designers, creating clear ownership, providing meaningful feedback, and helping each person build on their strengths and grow. You will foster a collaborative critique culture and create the conditions for the team to consistently deliver high-quality work.
  • Own the end-to-end product experience. You will be accountable for the quality, consistency, and coherence of the Clinical Platform Group product experience across clinical and administrative workflows. You will establish and uphold a high design standard, incorporating accessibility and clinical safety considerations into how experiences are designed and delivered.
  • Shape AI-assisted experiences. You will set the design direction for how AI is integrated into clinical workflows, including how suggestions are surfaced, confidence and provenance are communicated, and clinicians remain in control. You will help ensure AI-enabled experiences are practical, intuitive, and designed around the realities of clinical care.
  • Strengthen how Design, Product, and Engineering work together. You will partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to bring design into problem definition, discovery, refinement, and delivery. You will improve handoffs and feedback loops so requirements, designs, edge cases, and intended experiences are clearly understood and carried through to what is released.
  • Evolve design practices and systems. You will refine the design process from intake and discovery through critique, handoff, and design QA, keeping it structured without creating unnecessary complexity. You will champion the design system, patterns, documentation, and tools that help the team work efficiently and deliver a consistent experience.
  • Bring users closer to product decisions. You will establish a sustainable approach to user research, including interviews and engagement with clinics, and ensure insights are shared effectively across Design, Product, and Engineering. You will help turn what the team learns from clinicians and customers into meaningful improvements to the product and roadmap.

What you bring:

  • The design leadership experience. You have experience leading and developing product designers, including coaching, providing meaningful feedback, supporting career development, and managing performance. You know how to assess the strengths of an established team, build trust, and create the clarity and support people need to do their best work.
  • The product design expertise. You have designed and shipped complex, workflow-heavy software where usability, accuracy, and attention to detail matter. You bring strong design judgment and can critically evaluate work, challenge assumptions, and raise the quality and consistency of the user experience without imposing a rigid design philosophy.
  • The ability to evolve a design practice. You have improved how a design team operates, whether through stronger discovery and research practices, critique and review, design systems, handoffs, or design QA. You can introduce structure without unnecessary process and understand how to measure whether changes are making the team and the product better.
  • The cross-functional approach. You have worked closely with Product and Engineering teams in an agile product environment and understand how design fits into discovery, backlog refinement, sprint planning, development, and release. You can influence peers and senior stakeholders, communicate design decisions and trade-offs clearly, and build alignment around the user experience.
  • The curiosity for AI-enabled design. You are comfortable exploring AI-assisted design tools and bring a thoughtful perspective on where they can improve speed and effectiveness without compromising craft or consistency. Experience designing AI or LLM-powered products, including human-in-the-loop experiences, would be an asset.
  • The adaptability. You design for the needs of the people using the product rather than following a single definition of what good UX should look like. You can work with complex, information-dense experiences and balance user needs, accessibility, technical constraints, and the realities of the environment in which the product is used. Experience in healthcare, EMR/EHR products, or another regulated environment is an asset.

Why join us?

WELLSTAR is a leading healthcare technology company dedicated to reshaping healthcare through digital enablement. We provide a comprehensive, holistic solution for healthcare providers across Canada, with over 40% of practitioners currently using our products and services. Our solutions serve primary care physicians, specialist physicians, health systems, and public sector organizations through a comprehensive suite that includes billing and practice management systems, electronic medical records (EMRs), digital health applications, and digital health network solutions.

As a majority-owned subsidiary of WELL Health, WELLSTAR continues to drive innovation and transformation in the Canadian healthcare landscape, reducing administrative burden and empowering providers to deliver better patient outcomes through advanced technology solutions.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A virtual interview with the VP, Product Management focused on your design leadership experience, approach to developing and supporting a design team, and experience strengthening collaboration across Design, Product, and Engineering.
  • A final interview with the team focused on team dynamics, collaboration and how you would contribute to the broader team.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $120-150K. The salary will be determined based on several factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and the needs of the organization. At WELLSTAR, we are committed to fair and equitable compensation and aim to provide a competitive salary that reflects the value and expertise of the successful candidate.

Apply now.

Interested in applying but worried you don't have it all? At WELLSTAR, we know not everyone gains their experience following a traditional path. If you share our values, want to make a difference in healthcare technology solutions, and meet 70% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Express your interest here.

WELLSTAR is committed to supporting a diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We welcome and celebrate the diversity of applicants and team members across ability, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, and perspective. We strive to create an inclusive workplace where differences are celebrated and fuel our success. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates participating in all aspects of the selection process.

Supply Chain Manager

Animal Safety | Remote

About the Role

Neogen is seeking a Supply Chain Manager to lead material planning, inventory management, and supply chain execution across the Animal Safety business.

This role is responsible for leading a team of material planners, improving planning discipline, strengthening inventory performance, and ensuring product availability while balancing customer service, working capital, excess inventory, and scrap risk.

The Supply Chain Manager will partner closely with Operations, Procurement, Finance, Commercial, Manufacturing, Quality, suppliers, distributors, and other stakeholders to improve supply chain visibility, standardize processes, and drive stronger business outcomes.

The successful candidate will bring strong people leadership, analytical thinking, process improvement, and cross-functional partnership skills, with the ability to build structure and drive continuous improvement across the supply chain function.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

In this role, you will make an impact by:

  • Leading and developing a team of material planners responsible for supply planning, inventory management, and product availability
  • Providing clear direction, coaching, performance feedback, and development opportunities to team members
  • Establishing planning expectations, operating rhythms, and accountability across the material planning function
  • Overseeing analysis of forecast projections, demand changes, inventory requirements, and product delivery performance
  • Ensuring inventory levels support customer demand while minimizing backorders, excess inventory, obsolescence, and scrap risk
  • Driving improvements in forecast accuracy, inventory health, service levels, and planning execution
  • Reviewing supply and inventory data to identify risks, trends, constraints, and opportunities
  • Leading cross-functional efforts to resolve shortages, capacity constraints, supplier issues, and other supply disruptions
  • Partnering with Procurement, Operations, Manufacturing, Finance, Commercial, Quality, and other functions to align supply plans with business priorities
  • Building and maintaining effective relationships with suppliers, distributors, and other external partners
  • Supporting supplier performance discussions and identifying opportunities to improve supply continuity and reliability
  • Establishing and improving standardized supply chain processes, tools, and performance metrics
  • Supporting the development of stronger planning and inventory management capabilities across the Animal Safety organization
  • Monitoring key supply chain metrics and using data to drive decisions and corrective actions
  • Supporting new product introductions, product transitions, discontinuations, and lifecycle planning
  • Leading or supporting supply chain improvement initiatives focused on planning, inventory optimization, customer service, cost, and operational efficiency
  • Identifying supply chain risks and implementing mitigation strategies
  • Improving communication and visibility across planning, procurement, operations, and commercial teams
  • Providing recommendations to leadership regarding inventory, supply risk, service performance, and planning priorities
  • Promoting a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer focus

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, Logistics, Finance, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, material planning, demand planning, inventory management, procurement, or a related function
  • 2+ years of people leadership or direct team management experience
  • Experience leading material planning, supply planning, inventory management, or related supply chain activities
  • Experience analyzing demand, forecast, inventory, and supply data to support business decisions
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Operations, Procurement, Finance, Manufacturing, Commercial, or related teams
  • Experience identifying and resolving supply chain risks, shortages, inventory issues, or planning constraints
  • Experience using ERP, MRP, planning, or inventory management systems
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in animal health, life sciences, food safety, manufacturing, consumer products, or another product-based industry
  • Experience leading material planners, demand planners, buyers, or other supply chain professionals
  • Experience with supplier management and supply continuity planning
  • Experience with inventory optimization, working capital improvement, or obsolescence reduction
  • Experience supporting new product introductions and product lifecycle management
  • Experience building or standardizing supply chain processes within a growing or changing organization
  • Experience leading continuous improvement or operational excellence initiatives
  • Experience with advanced planning, forecasting, reporting, or analytics tools
  • Experience managing supply chain KPIs and performance metrics

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Strong people leadership and team development skills
  • Ability to build structure and improve processes in a changing environment
  • Strong business judgment and decision-making capability
  • Ability to balance customer service, inventory, cost, and supply risk
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills
  • Ability to influence across functions and organizational levels
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and make decisions with incomplete information
  • Continuous improvement mindset
  • Strong ownership and accountability

About the Company

Our client is a U.S.-based construction company specializing in the development of community parks, amenity centers, recreational spaces, monuments, and other outdoor environments for residential developers and communities.

The company works closely with project managers, construction managers, landscape architects, and other industry partners to deliver high-quality projects with a strong focus on execution, cost control, and operational excellence.

As the organization continues to manage a growing portfolio of active construction projects, it is strengthening its financial and project accounting capabilities to provide greater visibility into project performance and costs.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Job Cost Accountant to own the accuracy and integrity of job cost data across an active portfolio of construction projects.

This role is dedicated to project financial performance and will be responsible for running and reviewing job cost reports, maintaining accurate cost coding, reconciling project financial data between Sage 100 and Procore, managing the monthly Work in Progress (WIP) schedule, and partnering directly with Project Managers and Construction Managers.

This is not a passive reporting role. The Job Cost Accountant will be embedded with project teams and serve as a financial partner to operations, helping ensure that costs are accurately captured, forecasts remain current, and project leadership has reliable financial information for decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Job Cost Reporting & Accuracy

  • Run, review, and distribute weekly and monthly job cost reports from Sage 100 for all active projects.

  • Reconcile Procore commitments, change orders, and invoicing against Sage 100 job cost detail.

  • Identify financial variances and work with project teams to resolve discrepancies at the source.

  • Review cost coding for AP invoices, subcontractor billings, labor, and equipment charges before they close to the job.

  • Identify misallocated expenses and coordinate corrections with the appropriate project stakeholders.

  • Maintain an accurate cost code structure in collaboration with finance and project leadership.

  • Ensure job cost information rolls up accurately for financial reporting, project analysis, and estimating feedback.

Project Management & Construction Management Partnership

  • Conduct formal monthly job cost reviews with Project Managers and Construction Managers.

  • Review budget vs. actual costs, committed costs, job cost detail, and forecast-to-complete estimates.

  • Partner with project teams to identify and correct misallocated expenses.

  • Serve as a primary finance resource for questions related to job costs, cost code selection, and committed cost reconciliation.

  • Escalate recurring coding or accountability issues to finance and project leadership when appropriate.

WIP & Percentage of Completion

  • Own the monthly WIP schedule across all active projects.

  • Maintain accurate calculations for:

    • Cost to date

    • Estimated cost at completion

    • Percentage complete

    • Earned revenue

    • Over/under billings

  • Partner with Project Managers to validate monthly cost-to-complete estimates.

  • Identify and challenge outdated or unsupported project forecasts.

  • Deliver a clean, accurate, and defensible WIP package as part of the monthly financial close process.

Specialized Cost Tracking

  • Partner with project leadership to capture the true cost of specialized construction activities when deeper cost analysis is required.

  • Establish tracking approaches before activities begin, including appropriate cost codes, labor tracking, equipment capture, and reporting structure.

  • Ensure cost information is collected accurately in real time rather than reconstructed after project activities are completed.

  • Prepare actual-cost reporting that can support future estimating, purchasing, project planning, and strategic decision-making.

Systems, Reporting & Documentation

  • Work extensively in Sage 100 and Procore as the primary systems for project cost accounting.

  • Maintain accurate and consistent financial data across both systems.

  • Build and maintain Excel reporting workbooks summarizing job cost, WIP, committed cost, and project financial performance.

  • Use AI-enabled tools and services, where appropriate, to improve reporting, reconciliation, and document review processes.

  • Maintain organized documentation and strong data hygiene across project accounting workflows.

Required Qualifications

  • 3–6 years of job cost accounting experience with a general contractor, specialty contractor, or construction company.

  • Construction industry accounting experience is required.

  • Hands-on experience with construction job costing and project financial reporting.

  • Working proficiency with Sage 100 Contractor or Sage 100 construction job cost modules.

  • Working proficiency with Procore, including commitments, change orders, and invoicing.

  • Experience preparing and maintaining WIP schedules and percentage-of-completion calculations.

  • Strong understanding of cost codes, committed costs, project budgets, actual costs, and cost-to-complete forecasting.

  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup functions, reconciliations, and reporting workbooks.

  • Experience reconciling financial information across accounting and project management systems.

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

  • Ability to identify discrepancies, investigate root causes, and coordinate corrections with operational teams.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

  • Ability to work effectively with U.S.-based finance, project management, and construction teams in a fully remote environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience supporting multiple active construction projects simultaneously.

About EPR Fireworks

EPR is a leading provider of cloud-based unified records management and operations software for fire and emergency medical services agencies. Since its founding in 2016, EPR has established itself as a trusted technology partner to approximately 500 fire and EMS agencies across 35 states. The company's comprehensive, cloud-based platform delivers an integrated solution encompassing incident reporting, electronic patient care records, fire prevention, workforce management, equipment logistics, training and certifications, advanced analytics, and community engagement capabilities.

EPR's platform development follows a continuous feedback methodology, incorporating insights from fire chiefs, department officers, medical directors, inspectors, and frontline fire and EMS personnel. The company's team includes numerous former and current firefighters and EMTs, ensuring authentic industry perspective in product design and functionality. With NERIS V1 compatibility and over 270 pre-configured reports, EPR Fireworks provides customizable solutions supported by exceptional customer service. The platform's integrated architecture eliminates data silos while ensuring regulatory compliance with evolving requirements.

About the Opportunity

EPR is seeking a strategic and hands-on Growth Marketing Manager to own the programs and channels that turn marketing strategy into measurable growth. This role will lead integrated campaigns across events, webinars, email, lead generation, nurture, and other demand-generation programs, connecting marketing activity directly to engagement, qualified opportunities, and pipeline.

Events are a significant part of EPR's go-to-market strategy. This person will play a hands-on role in planning and executing conferences and industry events across the country and should be comfortable traveling throughout the year. The role extends well beyond event logistics: the Growth Marketing Manager will be responsible for turning events into campaigns through pre-event targeting and promotion, onsite engagement, and disciplined post-event follow-up.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable building a campaign strategy and rolling up their sleeves to execute it. This person will own programs from concept through measurement, coordinating audiences, messaging, channels, timelines, follow-up, and reporting.

EPR is looking for a curious, data-driven marketer who enjoys experimenting, moves quickly, and continually asks what is working, what is not, and what should happen next.


Requirements

Key Responsibilities Include:

·Event Marketing:Own marketing strategy and execution for EPR's conferences, tradeshows, and industry events, including planning, promotion, booth experience, onsite execution, lead capture, and post-event follow-up. Travel to key events throughout the year is required.

·Integrated Campaigns:Plan and execute multi-channel campaigns across email, events, webinars, digital channels, and other growth programs.

·Email & Nurture:Build and optimize email campaigns, audience segmentation, nurture programs, webinar communications, and event follow-up designed to move prospects through the buyer journey.

·Webinars & Digital Programs:Manage webinars and digital programs from promotion and registration through execution, follow-up, and performance analysis.

·Lead Generation & Conversion:Partner closely with Sales to improve the path from marketing engagement to qualified conversation and pipeline.

·Campaign Measurement:Track campaign performance, conversion rates, sourced and influenced pipeline, and channel effectiveness. Translate results into recommendations for future investment.

·Marketing Operations:Maintain strong campaign processes, audience lists, attribution, CRM hygiene, and reporting in partnership with Sales and Revenue Operations.

·Partner Marketing:Support select co-marketing opportunities with strategic partners, including joint launches, webinars, events, and campaigns when appropriate.

·Cross-Functional Collaboration:Work closely with Sales, Product, Customer Success, and the VP of Marketing to bring campaigns and go-to-market initiatives to market.

Critical Skills:

· 0-3 years of experience in growth marketing, demand generation, integrated marketing, event marketing, or B2B SaaS marketing.

·Demonstrated experience planning and executing multi-channel campaigns from strategy through measurement.

·Strong experience with B2B events and tradeshows, including planning, onsite execution, lead generation, and follow-up.

·Willingness and ability to travel throughout the year for industry conferences, events, and company initiatives.

·Strong email marketing and campaign management skills, including segmentation, nurture, testing, and performance analysis.

·Ability to connect marketing activity to measurable outcomes including engagement, qualified opportunities, pipeline, and revenue.

·Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, events, and deadlines simultaneously.

·Comfortable working within CRM, marketing automation, webinar, analytics, and campaign management platforms.

·Data-driven, curious, and comfortable testing new approaches and continuously improving performance.

The Ideal Candidate:

·Experience in B2B SaaS, GovTech, public safety, or another complex B2B market is preferred.

·A hands-on marketer who enjoys both planning the campaign and executing the details.

·Moves with urgency.You’re comfortable making decisions, executing quickly, and adjusting based on results rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

·Energized by events and comfortable representing EPR alongside customers, prospects, partners, and the Sales team.

·Understands that a successful event begins well before the booth opens and continues well after everyone goes home.

·Commercially minded and interested in how marketing ultimately contributes to pipeline and revenue.

·Organized enough to manage detailed execution while maintaining sight of the larger growth objective.

·Collaborative, low-ego teammate who communicates clearly, takes ownership, and follows through.

·Curious and tech-forward, with an interest in using automation and AI to improve marketing productivity and performance.

Job Summary:
We are seeking a seasoned Microservices Architect to lead the design and evolution of large-scale microservices ecosystems built on modern container platforms and cloud-native technology stacks. The role requires deep expertise in service decomposition, domain-driven design, distributed data management, and runtime concerns such as resilience, observability, and security at scale. The ideal candidate brings hands-on architectural leadership across complex transformations, with a clear point of view on when microservices are the right answer, how to evolve them safely, and how to keep the resulting estate maintainable over the long term.

  • Define microservices architecture standards, service boundaries, and decomposition strategies aligned with domain-driven design principles.
  • Lead the modernization of legacy monoliths into well-bounded, independently deployable services with clear ownership.
  • Design service communication patterns leveraging REST, gRPC, asynchronous messaging, and event streaming as appropriate.
  • Establish API contracts, schema governance, and versioning strategies that enable safe evolution of services over time.
  • Architect resilient distributed systems incorporating circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads, and graceful degradation patterns.
  • Define data ownership models, transactional boundaries, and patterns such as outbox, saga, and CQRS where appropriate.
  • Lead the design of platform capabilities including service mesh, API gateway, identity propagation, and shared observability.
  • Drive performance engineering, capacity planning, and scalability analysis across critical service domains.
  • Establish CI/CD, testing, and deployment standards optimized for high-frequency, low-risk service releases.
  • Define observability standards including structured logging, distributed tracing, and SLO-driven monitoring.
  • Collaborate with security teams to ensure zero-trust principles, secrets management, and runtime protection are embedded.
  • Mentor engineers and tech leads on microservices best practices and anti-pattern avoidance.
  • Lead architecture reviews and provide guidance on service design proposals across multiple teams.
  • Continuously evaluate emerging cloud-native technologies for adoption based on maturity and strategic fit.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related discipline.
  • 12 or more years of software engineering experience, with several years in architecture roles.
  • Deep expertise in microservices design, domain-driven design, and distributed systems patterns.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes, container orchestration, and service mesh technologies.
  • Proficiency in at least one major backend language such as Java, Go, or C#.
  • Strong understanding of API design, event-driven architectures, and asynchronous messaging.
  • Experience operating high-traffic, latency-sensitive systems in production.
  • Strong knowledge of cloud platforms and managed services across at least one major provider.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead architecture initiatives spanning multiple teams.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with platform engineering and internal developer platform construction.
  • Familiarity with Istio, Linkerd, Envoy, or comparable service mesh technologies.
  • Exposure to FinOps practices and cloud cost optimization at scale.

Whether you are a rising star with a track record of identifying trends before they break or an analytical powerhouse looking to transition into the fast-paced venture ecosystem, we care about your drive. If you have the persistence to manage massive deal pipelines, the research rigor to deconstruct complex protocols, and the communication skills to conduct high-level founder meetings, we will give you the platform to accelerate your career.

  • Analytical Rigor: You love numbers and raw data. You are entirely comfortable breaking down a complex business model or a protocol's transaction flows using hard logic.

  • Hyper-Availability: This isn't a 9-to-5. Markets shift fast and founders operate around the clock. You must be available 7 days a week to lock down opportunities, support portfolio needs, and keep deployment timelines moving.

Why Join Us?

We offer more than just an entry-level investment role; we offer a masterclass in the future of the digital economy.

  • High-Velocity Execution: You won't just be reviewing pitch decks; you will be helping to deploy capital into cutting-edge systems, gaining unparalleled insight into what makes a venture succeed.

  • Transferable Mastery: The skills you develop here—surgical market analysis, high-level deal structuring, and data-driven company building—are the most sought-after capabilities in the modern economy.

About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations.

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.

Role

Design how people use AI in real product workflows. This role focuses on building HCI interfaces where users can understand, guide, correct, and stay in control of AI systems that reason and act across multiple steps.

Current UX patterns are not enough for proactive AI products. You will help define new interaction models for how users work with AI, review progress, recover from mistakes, and build trust in the system.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design end-to-end user experiences for AI product surfaces, from concept to shipped product.

  • Create interaction patterns for human-AI workflows, including prompting, review, confirmation, correction, handoff, and recovery.

  • Design interfaces that help users understand what the AI is doing, what it knows, what it is unsure about, and what will happen next.

  • Turn complex, multi-step AI capabilities into flows that are clear, controllable, and usable in everyday contexts.

  • Work closely with product, engineering, and ML teams to define problems, test ideas, and ship quickly.

  • Produce wireframes, flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs for web and mobile.

  • Run lightweight user research and usability tests to identify friction, trust issues, and failure points.

  • Help define reusable HCI design patterns as the product and design system mature.

What You Will Need

  • Experience as a product designer or UX designer, with a portfolio across web or mobile products.

  • Strong skills in interaction design, information hierarchy, and prototyping.

  • Proficiency in Figma and fast iteration workflows.

  • Ability to simplify complex systems and turn unclear product behavior into clear user experiences.

  • Experience working closely with product managers and engineers in fast-moving teams.

  • Comfort working with ambiguity and shaping solutions before requirements are fully defined.

  • Good judgment on usability, edge cases, and failure handling.

  • Clear thinking about trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven experiences.

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

Interview process

For design roles, we expect candidates to submit a portfolio as part of the application process.

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2 rounds of interviews and a design assessment.

Applications are evaluated by our team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

Job Desceiption:

Certified Inpatient/Outpatient Medical Coding Specialist

Front-End Coding | Coding Denials | Claim Rejections

Position Summary

The Certified Coding Specialist is responsible for reviewing medical documentation and assigning accurate diagnosis and procedure codes for inpatient and outpatient facility services while ensuring compliance with ICD-10-CM/PCS, CPT, HCPCS, payer policies, and regulatory guidelines. This position also supports coding-related claim denials and front-end claim edits/rejections by identifying coding opportunities prior to claim submission and resolving post-adjudication coding issues. The ideal candidate possesses strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively with providers, CDI, billing, and revenue cycle teams to maximize coding accuracy and reimbursement.

Education & Certification

  • Required: Active CPC, COC, CCS, or CIC certification.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience coding both inpatient and outpatient facility accounts.
  • Experience reviewing coding-related denials and appeals.
  • Experience resolving front-end claim edits and payer rejections.
  • Knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payer reimbursement guidelines.
  • Experience using coding encoders and electronic medical record systems (e.g., 3M, TruCode, Epic, Meditech, Cerner).
  • Knowledge of DRG, APC, NCCI edits, and medical necessity guidelines.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years of inpatient and/or outpatient facility coding preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, HCPCS Level II, modifiers, DRGs/APCs.
  • Knowledge of NCCI edits, LCD/NCDs, CMS regulations, and Official Coding Guidelines.
  • Excellent communication and Microsoft Office skills.
  • Ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and work independently.

Primary Responsibilities – Front-End Coding

  • Review inpatient, outpatient, ED, observation, surgery, and ancillary records.
  • Assign accurate ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, HCPCS, and modifier codes.
  • Review coding edits and work queues prior to claim submission.
  • Validate documentation supports code assignment.
  • Query providers when documentation is incomplete or conflicting.
  • Maintain productivity and quality standards.
  • Participate in coding audits and education.

Coding Denials & Appeals

· Review coding-related payer denials.

· Perform root cause analysis.

  • Correct coding errors and recommend appeals.
  • Review denials involving medical necessity, bundling, modifiers, DRGs/APCs, sequencing, and procedures.
  • Collaborate with CDI, billing, providers, and revenue integrity.
  • Monitor denial trends and recommend improvements.

Front-End Claim Rejections

  • Review coding-related claim rejections before adjudication.
  • Correct coding errors causing claim rejections.
  • Validate diagnosis/procedure combinations and modifier usage.
  • Partner with billing to reduce preventable rejections.

· Track recurring rejection trends.

Compliance & Quality

· Maintain HIPAA compliance.

  • Remain current on coding and payer updates.
  • Follow CMS, AHIMA, AAPC, AMA, and payer guidance.
  • Meet departmental productivity and QA expectations. (95% or greater)

Team Collaboration

  • Work with Coding Leadership, CDI, Revenue Cycle, Revenue Integrity, Billing, and Providers.
  • Assist with education, process improvement, and mentoring.
  • Communicate coding and payer updates to the team.

Preferred Areas of Experience

· Inpatient Facility Coding

· Outpatient Facility Coding

· Emergency Department Coding

· Observation

· Same-Day Surgery

· Infusion & Injection Coding

· Medical Necessity Reviews

· DRG Validation

· Revenue Integrity

· Coding Denials

· Claim Rejections

jobs.excerpt: Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI.
jobs.description:
Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate analytics, machine learning, and AI agents with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack - empowering organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance.

The world’s leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube.

About the role

Dataiku is the platform for AI Success, helping organizations put AI to work across their business. The Growth team drives pipeline generation globally through paid media, content syndication, ABM, and marketing operations, and we're looking for a Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing to build and own the lifecycle function end to end.

You'll work closely with the VP of Digital & Growth and cross-functional partners across Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success, supporting a global organization across regions. We don't have a lifecycle function today. Email and nurture are secondary responsibilities inside other teams' jobs, so nobody owns what a prospect or customer hears from us, in what order, or how often. There are existing nurture workflows without a current owner and no single view of what runs where, so establishing that visibility is the first priority. You'll build the function from there: the strategy, the systems, the programs, and the team.

What you'll own

The lifecycle operating system

  • One authoritative email and lifecycle calendar across prospect, new-user and customer programs: what goes out, to whom, from which team, and when.
  • Frequency governance, suppression logic and deliverability standards, including being able to say how much of an audience a given send reaches.
  • Segmentation and audience standards, set with the web and marketing ops teams who manage list creation today.
  • A standard for what a lifecycle program needs before it launches: entry criteria, success metric, exit.

Prospect and new-user nurture

  • New-user onboarding and activation nurture: the sequences that move a first touch to an engaged, sales-ready account.
  • Account progression communication: the programs that move accounts from first engagement toward qualified opportunity.
  • Nurture designed around named-account cohorts, built alongside the integrated campaign work so the two don't duplicate each other.
  • Visibility for BDRs into what a lead has already received before they reach out.

Customer lifecycle, retention and expansion

You'll partner closely with Customer Success and Product on this.

  • Programmatic customer nurture: adoption, education, and the sequences that keep users active after initial deployment.
  • Retention and expansion programs, built on account signals rather than calendar cadence.

Automation, data and measurement

  • The lifecycle layer of the marketing automation stack end to end: HubSpot workflows, Salesforce integration, and account and intent data from 6sense.
  • Consolidating the existing nurture workflows into something documented and maintained.
  • Reporting lifecycle contribution in terms the business already uses: engagement progression, influenced pipeline, retention and expansion. You'll build your own reporting rather than wait for a dashboard.
  • The data quality this function depends on, with marketing ops: deliverability, consent, record hygiene.

AI and agentic workflows

  • Lifecycle work inside agentic workflows, rather than AI as a separate experiment. Lifecycle is one of the clearest applications: audience assembly, copy variation, program QA, performance summaries.
  • A standard for what a well-built lifecycle agent looks like, and where human in the loop is required.

Building the function

  • This is the lead role for a function that doesn't exist yet. You'll build the team as the function develops.
  • Getting the rest of the organization aligned on what you're building. Lifecycle touches Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in lifecycle, nurture, email or growth marketing in B2B, ideally enterprise software with long, multi-threaded buying cycles.
  • Hands-on marketing automation depth. You've built and owned complex nurture programs yourself. HubSpot or Marketo depth, Salesforce fluency, and real comfort with the data model under both.
  • Command of deliverability, frequency capping, suppression, consent and list hygiene. This role exists partly because nobody has owned these.
  • Experience on both sides of the lifecycle, prospect and customer. If your background covers one, tell us how you'd approach the other.
  • Fluency with intent and account data (6sense, Demandbase or similar), and a view on where it should drive program entry rather than only reporting.
  • Comfort building with AI, expected rather than optional. No engineering background needed. You should already be using LLMs in your own work, with a view on where they belong in lifecycle programs and where human in the loop is required.
  • Analytical strength. You can define a metric, instrument it, and defend it, including when the honest answer is that the current number isn't reliable.
  • Comfort with a build role: ambiguity, direct conversations about tradeoffs, and establishing a function through influence before you have a team.
  • Experience working across regions in a global organization.
  • Excellent written English. Other languages welcome, not required.

Why this role

Lifecycle is unowned at Dataiku today. This role defines it, reporting to the VP who owns the function, with a mandate to build the team behind it.

What are you waiting for!

At Dataiku, you'll be part of a journey to shape the ever-evolving world of AI. We're not just building a product; we're crafting the future of AI. If you're ready to make a significant impact in a company that values innovation, collaboration, and your personal growth, we can't wait to welcome you to Dataiku! And if you’d like to learn even more about working here, you can visit our Dataiku LinkedIn page.

jobs.description:
Senior Product Engineer

Company Overview

ActiveProspect is on a mission to make consent-based marketing the best channel for online customer acquisition. We provide marketers the products they need to acquire qualified customers at scale. Our platform is trusted by thousands of companies engaged in direct-to-consumer marketing, helping them save wasted spend, comply with ever-changing regulations, and manage a constantly evolving partner landscape. Our flagship product, TrustedForm, is used to certify over 1 billion opt-in digital customer leads every year and is the gold standard for documenting prior express written consent for TCPA compliance.

Job Summary

You own customer and business outcomes, not tickets. You work like a forward-deployed engineer: your home base is a core team, and you deploy into projects, initiatives, and pods where the problem is, ship the outcome across the full stack (React on the frontend, Node.js and Python services on AWS), then carry what you learned back so the next team moves faster.. The technical bar is high, but coding ability is the floor here, not the ceiling. What sets this role apart is judgment: knowing the smallest thing worth shipping, when to kill your own idea, and when AI output is good enough versus when to override it.

You'll move between your home team and the initiatives you deploy into, shipping early, talking to customers, and deciding fast.

Responsibilities

  • Own outcomes end-to-end, wherever you're deployed. Frame the problem, design it, ship it, own the metric. Descope to the cheapest version that works. Prototype in days.
  • Stay close to customers. Shadow sales and support, join advisory conversations, and let customer reality drive technical decisions. Propose what to build, defer, and kill.
  • Own your domain and share it. Its interfaces, reliability, performance, and security, including on-call for the systems you own. Consent and PII handling are central to customer trust. Bring patterns, tooling, and hard-won context back to the wider org rather than hoarding them.
  • Build and scale both the product surface and the platform beneath it. Ship responsive, accessible React interfaces with a strong UI/UX eye, back them with Node.js and Python services and APIs, and keep the cloud batch platform and data pipelines that deliver multi-tenant products reliable as they scale.
  • Architect AI-driven leverage. Build AI-assisted workflows that hold up, evolve the team's practices as tooling changes (Cursor, Claude Code, and whatever comes next), and look for product wins AI unlocks (smarter routing, anomaly detection, and more).
  • Multiply the teams you touch. Mentor on judgment and product sense, not just syntax. Write decision memos and ADRs. Enable Product and Design to self-serve.

Qualifications and Skills

  • A track record of shipping something end-to-end that you cared about and owning the outcome, not just the code.
  • Product judgment: pushing back on a bad spec, proposing the cheapest experiment, descoping well, and collaborating with Product to suggest solutions rather than waiting for a fully specced ticket.
  • Comfort embedding with unfamiliar teams and codebases, getting productive fast, and leaving them better than you found them.
  • Deep full-stack expertise: React (component lifecycle, state management, rendering optimization), JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern CSS on the frontend; Node.js and Python services, RESTful APIs, and asynchronous data handling on the backend.
  • Cloud and data-pipeline depth: AWS core services (Lambda, EC2, S3, DynamoDB, API Gateway) and cloud batch / workflow orchestration (Step Functions, Airflow, or similar) to deliver multi-tenant batch products and data solutions reliably at scale.
  • A strong UI/UX eye: you turn wireframes, mockups, and ambiguous requirements into intuitive, accessible, user-centric journeys.
  • Strong systems design judgment in ambiguous contexts, and a security mindset aligned with sensitive consumer data and compliance.
  • Fluency building your own AI-assisted workflows and reading AI output critically. Daily use of AI-native tools (Cursor, Claude Code) and precise prompting across OpenAI and Claude models, with the judgment to know when to trust output, how to review it for hidden bugs and security issues, and when to override it.
  • Clear written and verbal communication. Mentorship experience. 5-10% travel.

How It Works

You'll report to an Engineering Manager who owns several teams and stays out of their daily flow. As you embed, you'll often act as the player-coach Tech Lead, owning technical direction while the EM owns delivery health and stakeholder alignment across the group.

Success looks like movement in a user or business metric you/your team owns, high-value work deliberately not built, decisions made fast, and teams that move faster after you've worked with them, not just while you're there.

Reports To

Engineering Manager

jobs.excerpt: Erfahrung weitergeben.  Zukunft gestalten. Jede berufliche Erfahrung kann den Unterschied machen.
jobs.description:
Erfahrung weitergeben. Zukunft gestalten.

Jede berufliche Erfahrung kann den Unterschied machen. Genau deshalb suchen wir Menschen, die ihr Wissen weitergeben und die berufliche Weiterbildung aktiv mitgestalten möchten.

Warum TÜV Seminare Saarland?

Seit vielen Jahren begleiten wir Unternehmen und Fachkräfte mit hochwertigen Weiterbildungsangeboten in den Bereichen Technik, Management und Sicherheit. Unsere Seminare verbinden aktuelles Fachwissen mit einem hohen Praxisbezug – getragen von Expertinnen und Experten, die ihre Erfahrungen aus dem Berufsalltag einbringen.

Als Teil unseres Expertenkreises profitieren Sie von einer professionellen Organisation, einem etablierten Kundenstamm und einem starken Netzwerk. Sie konzentrieren sich auf das, was Sie am besten können: Ihr Wissen weitergeben. Wir übernehmen den Rest.

Aufgaben

Durchführung von Seminaren im Bereich Maschinen in einem oder mehreren der nachfolgenden Schwerpunktbereiche:

  • Fortbildung zum Erhalt der Prüfsachkunde von Zentrifugen nach TRBS 1203 in Verbindung mit Fachbereich Aktuell FB RCI-025
  • Zur Prüfung befähigte Person von Zentrifugen nach TRBS 1203 in Verbindung mit Fachbereich Aktuell FB RCI-025

Qualifikation

Fachliche Qualifikation (zwingend erforderlich)

Ein Dozent muss zwingend eine tiefgehende Fach- und Sachkunde nachweisen. Je nach Komplexität der Zentrifugen (z. B. Laborzentrifugen, Industrie- und Großzentrifugen in der Chemie oder Verfahrenstechnik) wird Folgendes gefordert:

  • Akademischer/Beruflicher Abschluss: Ein abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Maschinenbau, Verfahrenstechnik, Biotechnologie, Physik oder eine Qualifikation als Techniker oder Industriemeister im relevanten Fachgebiet.
  • Sicherheits-Expertise: Exzellente Kenntnisse der gesetzlichen Vorgaben wie der Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV), der TRBS 1203 (Technische Regeln für Betriebssicherheit) sowie der berufsgenossenschaftlichen Regelwerke (z. B. DGUV Regel 100-500, Kapitel 2.11 zu Zentrifugen).
  • Prüfkompetenz: Der Dozent muss in der Regel selbst die Kriterien einer "Zur Prüfung befähigten Person für Zentrifugen" erfüllen, um dieses Wissen rechtssicher an zukünftige Prüfer weiterzugeben.
  • Praxisnahe Tätigkeit: Mehrjährige, zeitnahe berufliche Erfahrung in der Konstruktion, dem Betrieb, der Wartung oder der sicherheitstechnischen Prüfung von Zentrifugen. Reine Theorie reicht bei technischen Schulungen selten aus.
  • Gefährdungsbeurteilung: Erfahrung in der Durchführung und Erstellung von Gefährdungsbeurteilungen speziell für den physikalischen Betrieb von Zentrifugen (z. B. Beherrschung von Risiken durch Fliehkräfte, Unwuchten und Materialermüdung).

Didaktische und Pädagogische Kompetenz

Über Fachwissen hinaus, müssen Sie als Dozent in der Lage sein, Lerninhalte verständlich zu vermitteln:

  • Pädagogische Eignung: Erfahrung in der Erwachsenenbildung, nachweisbar durch Train-the-Trainer-Zertifikate oder eine Ausbildereignungsprüfung (AdA-Schein) und die Fähigkeit, theoretische Vorschriften (wie Schadensszenarien oder Gefährdungsbeurteilungen) anhand von realen Fallbeispielen und Praxisübungen verständlich zu erklären.

Benefits

  • Flexibles Arbeiten auf Honorarbasis
  • Attraktive VergütungAngenehme Atmosphäre, in der Arbeiten Spaß macht
  • Hoch motiviertes Team, für das Hilfsbereitschaft selbstverständlich ist
  • Möglichkeiten zur persönlichen und fachlichen Weiterentwicklung

Interesse an einer Zusammenarbeit?

Wenn Sie Interesse an dieser spannenden Herausforderung haben, senden Sie bitte Ihre Bewerbungsunterlagen (Lebenslauf, Kurzvita, relevante Zertifikate) an uns. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung!

Ihr Wissen verdient eine Bühne.

About the Company

Our client is a U.S.-based construction company specializing in the development of community parks, amenity centers, recreational spaces, monuments, and other outdoor environments for residential developers and communities.

The company works closely with project managers, construction managers, landscape architects, and other industry partners to deliver high-quality projects with a strong focus on execution, cost control, and operational excellence.

As the organization continues to manage a growing portfolio of active construction projects, it is strengthening its financial and project accounting capabilities to provide greater visibility into project performance and costs.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Job Cost Accountant to own the accuracy and integrity of job cost data across an active portfolio of construction projects.

This role is dedicated to project financial performance and will be responsible for running and reviewing job cost reports, maintaining accurate cost coding, reconciling project financial data between Sage 100 and Procore, managing the monthly Work in Progress (WIP) schedule, and partnering directly with Project Managers and Construction Managers.

This is not a passive reporting role. The Job Cost Accountant will be embedded with project teams and serve as a financial partner to operations, helping ensure that costs are accurately captured, forecasts remain current, and project leadership has reliable financial information for decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Job Cost Reporting & Accuracy

  • Run, review, and distribute weekly and monthly job cost reports from Sage 100 for all active projects.

  • Reconcile Procore commitments, change orders, and invoicing against Sage 100 job cost detail.

  • Identify financial variances and work with project teams to resolve discrepancies at the source.

  • Review cost coding for AP invoices, subcontractor billings, labor, and equipment charges before they close to the job.

  • Identify misallocated expenses and coordinate corrections with the appropriate project stakeholders.

  • Maintain an accurate cost code structure in collaboration with finance and project leadership.

  • Ensure job cost information rolls up accurately for financial reporting, project analysis, and estimating feedback.

Project Management & Construction Management Partnership

  • Conduct formal monthly job cost reviews with Project Managers and Construction Managers.

  • Review budget vs. actual costs, committed costs, job cost detail, and forecast-to-complete estimates.

  • Partner with project teams to identify and correct misallocated expenses.

  • Serve as a primary finance resource for questions related to job costs, cost code selection, and committed cost reconciliation.

  • Escalate recurring coding or accountability issues to finance and project leadership when appropriate.

WIP & Percentage of Completion

  • Own the monthly WIP schedule across all active projects.

  • Maintain accurate calculations for:

    • Cost to date

    • Estimated cost at completion

    • Percentage complete

    • Earned revenue

    • Over/under billings

  • Partner with Project Managers to validate monthly cost-to-complete estimates.

  • Identify and challenge outdated or unsupported project forecasts.

  • Deliver a clean, accurate, and defensible WIP package as part of the monthly financial close process.

Specialized Cost Tracking

  • Partner with project leadership to capture the true cost of specialized construction activities when deeper cost analysis is required.

  • Establish tracking approaches before activities begin, including appropriate cost codes, labor tracking, equipment capture, and reporting structure.

  • Ensure cost information is collected accurately in real time rather than reconstructed after project activities are completed.

  • Prepare actual-cost reporting that can support future estimating, purchasing, project planning, and strategic decision-making.

Systems, Reporting & Documentation

  • Work extensively in Sage 100 and Procore as the primary systems for project cost accounting.

  • Maintain accurate and consistent financial data across both systems.

  • Build and maintain Excel reporting workbooks summarizing job cost, WIP, committed cost, and project financial performance.

  • Use AI-enabled tools and services, where appropriate, to improve reporting, reconciliation, and document review processes.

  • Maintain organized documentation and strong data hygiene across project accounting workflows.

Required Qualifications

  • 3–6 years of job cost accounting experience with a general contractor, specialty contractor, or construction company.

  • Construction industry accounting experience is required.

  • Hands-on experience with construction job costing and project financial reporting.

  • Working proficiency with Sage 100 Contractor or Sage 100 construction job cost modules.

  • Working proficiency with Procore, including commitments, change orders, and invoicing.

  • Experience preparing and maintaining WIP schedules and percentage-of-completion calculations.

  • Strong understanding of cost codes, committed costs, project budgets, actual costs, and cost-to-complete forecasting.

  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup functions, reconciliations, and reporting workbooks.

  • Experience reconciling financial information across accounting and project management systems.

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

  • Ability to identify discrepancies, investigate root causes, and coordinate corrections with operational teams.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

  • Ability to work effectively with U.S.-based finance, project management, and construction teams in a fully remote environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience supporting multiple active construction projects simultaneously.

  • Experience working directly with Project Managers and Construction Managers on monthly financial reviews.

  • Knowledge of construction revenue recognition and percentage-of-completion accounting.

  • Experience with AP coding, subcontractor billing, change orders, commitments, and construction cost controls.

  • Experience using AI or automation tools to improve accounting, reconciliation, or reporting workflows.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will ensure that project financial data is accurate, timely, and actionable. Project Managers and Construction Managers will have a reliable financial partner who understands their projects, WIP reporting will be accurate and defensible, cost coding issues will be identified and corrected quickly, and leadership will have greater visibility into the true financial performance of every active project.

The Proposal Manager will ingest solicitation materials, organize requirements, assemble the appropriate internal response team, identify required content, and determine which materials may be adapted from prior responses or approved content libraries.
